6510.label: Judges 1:1
6510.text: And after the death of Joshua it came about that the sons of Israel proceeded to inquire of Jehovah, saying: “Who of us will go up first to the Caʹnaan·ites to fight against them?”

6511.label: Judges 1:2
6511.text: To this Jehovah said: “Judah will go up. Look! I shall certainly give the land into his hand.”

6512.label: Judges 1:3
6512.text: Then Judah said to Simʹe·on his brother: “Come up with me into my lot and let us fight against the Caʹnaan·ites, and I myself in turn will go with you into your lot.” Accordingly Simʹe·on went with him.

6513.label: Judges 1:4
6513.text: With that Judah went on up and Jehovah gave the Caʹnaan·ites and the Perʹiz·zites into their hands, so that they defeated them in Beʹzek, ten thousand men.

6514.label: Judges 1:5
6514.text: When they found A·doʹni-beʹzek in Beʹzek, then they fought against him and defeated the Caʹnaan·ites and the Perʹiz·zites.

6515.label: Judges 1:6
6515.text: When A·doʹni-beʹzek took to flight, then they went chasing after him and got hold of him and cut off the thumbs of his hands and the great toes of his feet.

6516.label: Judges 1:7
6516.text: At this A·doʹni-beʹzek said: “There have been seventy kings with the thumbs of their hands and the great toes of their feet cut off picking up food under my table. Just the way I have done, so God has repaid me.” After that they brought him to Jerusalem and he died there.

6517.label: Judges 1:8
6517.text: Furthermore, the sons of Judah carried on war against Jerusalem and got to capture it, and they went striking it with the edge of the sword, and the city they consigned to the fire.

6518.label: Judges 1:9
6518.text: And afterward the sons of Judah went down to fight against the Caʹnaan·ites inhabiting the mountainous region and the Negʹeb and the She·pheʹlah.

6519.label: Judges 1:10
6519.text: So Judah marched against the Caʹnaan·ites who were dwelling in Heʹbron (now the name of Heʹbron before that was Kirʹi·ath-arʹba), and they went striking down Sheʹshai and A·hiʹman and Talʹmai.

6520.label: Judges 1:11
6520.text: And they marched on from there against the inhabitants of Deʹbir. (Now the name of Deʹbir before that was Kirʹi·ath-seʹpher.)

6521.label: Judges 1:12
6521.text: Then Caʹleb said: “Whoever strikes Kirʹi·ath-seʹpher and does capture it, why, I will give him Achʹsah my daughter as a wife.”

6522.label: Judges 1:13
6522.text: And Othʹni·el the son of Keʹnaz, Caʹleb’s younger brother, got to capture it. For that he gave him Achʹsah his daughter as a wife.

6523.label: Judges 1:14
6523.text: And it came about that while she was going home, she kept inciting him to ask a field from her father. Then she clapped her hands while upon the ass. At this Caʹleb said to her: “What do you want?”

6524.label: Judges 1:15
6524.text: So she said to him: “Do grant me a blessing, for it is a southern piece of land you have given me, and you must give me Gulʹloth-maʹim.” Accordingly Caʹleb gave her Upper Gulʹloth and Lower Gulʹloth.

6525.label: Judges 1:16
6525.text: And the sons of the Kenʹite, whose son-in-law Moses was, came up out of the city of palm trees with the sons of Judah to the wilderness of Judah, which is to the south of Aʹrad. Then they went and took up dwelling with the people.

6526.label: Judges 1:17
6526.text: But Judah marched on with Simʹe·on his brother, and they proceeded to strike the Caʹnaan·ites inhabiting Zeʹphath and to devote it to destruction. Hence the name of the city was called Horʹmah.

6527.label: Judges 1:18
6527.text: After that Judah captured Gaʹza and its territory and Ashʹke·lon and its territory and Ekʹron and its territory.

6528.label: Judges 1:19
6528.text: And Jehovah continued with Judah, so that he took possession of the mountainous region, but he could not dispossess the inhabitants of the low plain, because they had war chariots with iron scythes.

6529.label: Judges 1:20
6529.text: When they gave Caʹleb Heʹbron, just as Moses had promised, then he drove out from there the three sons of Aʹnak.

6530.label: Judges 1:21
6530.text: And the sons of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebʹu·sites inhabiting Jerusalem; but the Jebʹu·sites keep on dwelling with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem down to this day.

6531.label: Judges 1:22
6531.text: Meantime the house of Joseph itself also went up against Bethʹel, and Jehovah was with them.

6532.label: Judges 1:23
6532.text: And the house of Joseph began to spy on Bethʹel (incidentally, the name of the city before that was Luz),

6533.label: Judges 1:24
6533.text: and the watchers got to see a man going out of the city. So they said to him: “Show us, please, the way to get into the city, and we shall certainly exercise kindness toward you.”

6534.label: Judges 1:25
6534.text: Accordingly the man showed them the way to get into the city; and they went striking the city with the edge of the sword, but the man and all his family they let go.

6535.label: Judges 1:26
6535.text: Upon that the man went to the land of the Hitʹtites and built a city and called its name Luz. That is its name down to this day.

6536.label: Judges 1:27
6536.text: And Ma·nasʹseh did not take possession of Beth-sheʹan and its dependent towns and Taʹa·nach and its dependent towns and the inhabitants of Dor and its dependent towns and the inhabitants of Ibʹle·am and its dependent towns and the inhabitants of Me·gidʹdo and its dependent towns, but the Caʹnaan·ites persisted in dwelling in this land.

6537.label: Judges 1:28
6537.text: And it came about that Israel grew strong and proceeded to set the Caʹnaan·ites to forced labor, and they did not drive them out completely.

6538.label: Judges 1:29
6538.text: Neither did Eʹphra·im drive out the Caʹnaan·ites who were dwelling in Geʹzer, but the Caʹnaan·ites continued to dwell in among them in Geʹzer.

6539.label: Judges 1:30
6539.text: Zebʹu·lun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitʹron and the inhabitants of Naʹha·lol, but the Caʹnaan·ites continued to dwell in among them and came to be subject to forced labor.

6540.label: Judges 1:31
6540.text: Ashʹer did not drive out the inhabitants of Acʹco and the inhabitants of Siʹdon and Ahʹlab and Achʹzib and Helʹbah and Aʹphik and Reʹhob.

6541.label: Judges 1:32
6541.text: And the Ashʹer·ites continued to dwell in among the Caʹnaan·ites inhabiting the land, because they did not drive them out.

6542.label: Judges 1:33
6542.text: Naphʹta·li did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-sheʹmesh and the inhabitants of Beth-aʹnath, but they continued to dwell in among the Caʹnaan·ites inhabiting the land; and the inhabitants of Beth-sheʹmesh and of Beth-aʹnath became theirs for forced labor.

6543.label: Judges 1:34
6543.text: And the Amʹor·ites kept pressing the sons of Dan into the mountainous region, for they did not allow them to come down into the low plain.

6544.label: Judges 1:35
6544.text: So the Amʹor·ites persisted in dwelling in Mount Heʹres and in Aiʹja·lon and Sha·alʹbim. But the hand of the house of Joseph got to be so heavy that they were forced into task work.

6545.label: Judges 1:36
6545.text: And the territory of the Amʹor·ites was from the ascent of A·krabʹbim, from Seʹla upward.

6546.label: Judges 2:1
6546.text: Then Jehovah’s angel went up from Gilʹgal to Boʹchim and said: “I proceeded to bring YOU up out of Egypt and to bring YOU into the land about which I swore to YOUR forefathers. Furthermore, I said, ‘Never shall I break my covenant with YOU.

6547.label: Judges 2:2
6547.text: And for YOUR part, YOU must not conclude a covenant with the inhabitants of this land. Their altars YOU should pull down.’ But YOU have not listened to my voice. Why have YOU done this?

6548.label: Judges 2:3
6548.text: So I, in turn, have said, ‘I shall not drive them away from before YOU, and they must become snares to YOU, and their gods will serve as a lure to YOU.’”

6549.label: Judges 2:4
6549.text: And it came about that as soon as Jehovah’s angel had spoken these words to all the sons of Israel, the people began to raise their voices and weep.

6550.label: Judges 2:5
6550.text: Hence they called the name of that place Boʹchim. And they proceeded to sacrifice there to Jehovah.

6551.label: Judges 2:6
6551.text: When Joshua sent the people away, then the sons of Israel went their way, each to his inheritance, to take possession of the land.

6552.label: Judges 2:7
6552.text: And the people continued to serve Jehovah all the days of Joshua and all the days of the older men who extended their days after Joshua and who had seen all of Jehovah’s great work that he did for Israel.

6553.label: Judges 2:8
6553.text: Then Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Jehovah, died at the age of a hundred and ten years.

6554.label: Judges 2:9
6554.text: So they buried him in the territory of his inheritance in Timʹnath-heʹres in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im, on the north of Mount Gaʹash.

6555.label: Judges 2:10
6555.text: And all that generation too were gathered to their fathers, and another generation began to rise after them that did not know Jehovah or the work that he had done for Israel.

6556.label: Judges 2:11
6556.text: And the sons of Israel fell to doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah and serving the Baʹals.

6557.label: Judges 2:12
6557.text: Thus they abandoned Jehovah the God of their fathers who had brought them out of the land of Egypt and went following other gods from among the gods of the peoples who were all around them and they began bowing down to them, so that they offended Jehovah.

6558.label: Judges 2:13
6558.text: Thus they abandoned Jehovah and took up serving Baʹal and the Ashʹto·reth images.

6559.label: Judges 2:14
6559.text: At this Jehovah’s anger blazed against Israel, so that he gave them into the hands of the pillagers, and they began to pillage them; and he proceeded to sell them into the hand of their enemies round about, and they were no longer able to stand before their enemies.

6560.label: Judges 2:15
6560.text: Everywhere that they went out, the hand of Jehovah proved to be against them for calamity, just as Jehovah had spoken and just as Jehovah had sworn to them; and they got to be in very sore straits.

6561.label: Judges 2:16
6561.text: So Jehovah would raise up judges, and they would save them out of the hand of their pillagers.

6562.label: Judges 2:17
6562.text: And even to their judges they did not listen, but they had immoral intercourse with other gods and went bowing down to them. They quickly turned aside from the way in which their forefathers had walked by obeying the commandments of Jehovah. They did not do like that.

6563.label: Judges 2:18
6563.text: And when Jehovah did raise up judges for them, Jehovah proved to be with the judge, and he saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for Jehovah would feel regret over their groaning because of their oppressors and those who were shoving them around.

6564.label: Judges 2:19
6564.text: And it occurred that when the judge died they would turn around and act more ruinously than their fathers by walking after other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They did not refrain from their practices and their stubborn behavior.

6565.label: Judges 2:20
6565.text: Finally Jehovah’s anger blazed against Israel and he said: “For the reason that this nation have overstepped my covenant that I commanded their forefathers and have not listened to my voice,

6566.label: Judges 2:21
6566.text: I too, for my part, shall not drive out again from before them a single one of the nations that Joshua left behind when he died,

6567.label: Judges 2:22
6567.text: in order by them to test Israel, whether they will be keepers of Jehovah’s way by walking in it just as their fathers kept it, or not.”

6568.label: Judges 2:23
6568.text: Accordingly Jehovah let these nations stay by not driving them out quickly, and he did not give them into Joshua’s hand.

6569.label: Judges 3:1
6569.text: Now these are the nations that Jehovah let stay so as by them to test Israel, that is, all those who had not experienced any of the wars of Caʹnaan;

6570.label: Judges 3:2
6570.text: it was only in order for the generations of the sons of Israel to have the experience, so as to teach them war, that is, only those who before that had not experienced such things:

6571.label: Judges 3:3
6571.text: The five axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines, and all the Caʹnaan·ites, even the Si·doʹni·ans and the Hiʹvites inhabiting Mount Lebʹa·non from Mount Baʹal-herʹmon as far as to the entering in of Haʹmath.

6572.label: Judges 3:4
6572.text: And they kept serving as agents to test Israel so as to know whether they would obey Jehovah’s commandments that he had commanded their fathers by means of Moses.

6573.label: Judges 3:5
6573.text: And the sons of Israel dwelt in among the Caʹnaan·ites, the Hitʹtites and the Amʹor·ites and the Perʹiz·zites and the Hiʹvites and the Jebʹu·sites.

6574.label: Judges 3:6
6574.text: And they proceeded to take their daughters as wives for themselves, and their own daughters they gave to their sons, and they took up serving their gods.

6575.label: Judges 3:7
6575.text: So the sons of Israel did what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, and they were forgetful of Jehovah their God and went serving the Baʹals and the sacred poles.

6576.label: Judges 3:8
6576.text: At this Jehovah’s anger blazed against Israel, so that he sold them into the hand of Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim the king of Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a; and the sons of Israel continued to serve Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim eight years.

6577.label: Judges 3:9
6577.text: And the sons of Israel began to call to Jehovah for aid. Then Jehovah raised a savior up for the sons of Israel that he might save them, Othʹni·el the son of Keʹnaz, the younger brother of Caʹleb.

6578.label: Judges 3:10
6578.text: The spirit of Jehovah now came upon him, and he became the judge of Israel. When he went out to battle, then Jehovah gave Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim the king of Syria into his hand so that his hand overpowered Cuʹshan-rish·a·thaʹim.

6579.label: Judges 3:11
6579.text: After that the land had no disturbance for forty years. Eventually Othʹni·el the son of Keʹnaz died.

6580.label: Judges 3:12
6580.text: And once again the sons of Israel went doing what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. At that Jehovah let Egʹlon the king of Moʹab grow strong against Israel, because they did what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes.

6581.label: Judges 3:13
6581.text: Furthermore, he gathered against them the sons of Amʹmon and Amʹa·lek. Then they went and struck Israel and took possession of the city of palm trees.

6582.label: Judges 3:14
6582.text: And the sons of Israel continued to serve Egʹlon the king of Moʹab eighteen years.

6583.label: Judges 3:15
6583.text: And the sons of Israel began to call to Jehovah for aid. So Jehovah raised up for them a savior, Eʹhud the son of Geʹra, a Benʹja·mite, a left-handed man. In time the sons of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Egʹlon the king of Moʹab.

6584.label: Judges 3:16
6584.text: Meanwhile Eʹhud made a sword for himself, and it had two edges, its length being a cubit. Then he girded it underneath his garment upon his right thigh.

6585.label: Judges 3:17
6585.text: And he proceeded to present the tribute to Egʹlon the king of Moʹab. Now Egʹlon was a very fat man.

6586.label: Judges 3:18
6586.text: And it came about that when he had finished presenting the tribute, he at once sent the people away, the bearers of the tribute.

6587.label: Judges 3:19
6587.text: And he himself turned back at the quarries that were at Gilʹgal, and he proceeded to say: “I have a secret word for you, O king.” So he said: “Keep silence!” With that all those who were standing by him went on out from him.

6588.label: Judges 3:20
6588.text: And Eʹhud came to him as he was sitting in his cool roof chamber that he had to himself. And Eʹhud went on to say: “A word of God I have for you.” At that he rose up from his throne.

6589.label: Judges 3:21
6589.text: Then Eʹhud thrust in his left hand and took the sword off his right thigh and plunged it into his belly.

6590.label: Judges 3:22
6590.text: And the handle kept going in also after the blade so that the fat closed in over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly, and the fecal matter began to come out.

6591.label: Judges 3:23
6591.text: And Eʹhud proceeded to go out through the air hole, but he closed the doors of the roof chamber behind him and locked them.

6592.label: Judges 3:24
6592.text: And he himself went out. And his servants came and began looking, and there the doors of the roof chamber were locked. So they said: “He is just easing nature in the cool interior room.”

6593.label: Judges 3:25
6593.text: And they kept waiting until they were ashamed, and, look! there was no one opening the doors of the roof chamber. At this they took the key and opened them, and, look! their lord was fallen to the earth dead!

6594.label: Judges 3:26
6594.text: As for Eʹhud, he escaped while they were lingering, and he himself passed by the quarries and made his escape to Se·iʹrah.

6595.label: Judges 3:27
6595.text: And it came about that when he got there he began blowing the horn in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im; and the sons of Israel began going down with him out of the mountainous region, he being at their head.

6596.label: Judges 3:28
6596.text: Then he said to them: “Follow me, because Jehovah has given YOUR enemies, the Moʹab·ites, into YOUR hand.” And they went following him and got to capture the fords of the Jordan against the Moʹab·ites, and they did not allow anybody to pass over.

6597.label: Judges 3:29
6597.text: And at that time they went striking down Moʹab, about ten thousand men, every one robust and every one a valiant man; and not a single one escaped.

6598.label: Judges 3:30
6598.text: And Moʹab came to be subdued on that day under Israel’s hand; and the land had no further disturbance for eighty years.

6599.label: Judges 3:31
6599.text: And after him there proved to be Shamʹgar the son of Aʹnath, and he went striking down the Phi·lisʹtines, six hundred men, with a cattle goad; and he too got to save Israel.

6600.label: Judges 4:1
6600.text: Then the sons of Israel again began to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes now that Eʹhud was dead.

6601.label: Judges 4:2
6601.text: So Jehovah sold them into the hand of Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan, who reigned in Haʹzor; and the chief of his army was Sisʹe·ra, and he was dwelling in Ha·roʹsheth of the nations.

6602.label: Judges 4:3
6602.text: And the sons of Israel began to cry out to Jehovah, because he had nine hundred war chariots with iron scythes, and he himself oppressed the sons of Israel with harshness twenty years.

6603.label: Judges 4:4
6603.text: Now Debʹo·rah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapʹpi·doth, was judging Israel at that particular time.

6604.label: Judges 4:5
6604.text: And she was dwelling under Debʹo·rah’s palm tree between Raʹmah and Bethʹel in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im; and the sons of Israel would go up to her for judgment.

6605.label: Judges 4:6
6605.text: And she proceeded to send and call Baʹrak the son of A·binʹo·am out of Keʹdesh-naphʹta·li and to say to him: “Has not Jehovah the God of Israel given the command? ‘Go and you must spread yourself out on Mount Taʹbor, and you must take with you ten thousand men out of the sons of Naphʹta·li and out of the sons of Zebʹu·lun.

6606.label: Judges 4:7
6606.text: And I shall certainly draw to you at the torrent valley of Kiʹshon Sisʹe·ra the chief of Jaʹbin’s army and his war chariots and his crowd, and I shall indeed give him into your hand.’”

6607.label: Judges 4:8
6607.text: At this Baʹrak said to her: “If you will go with me, I also shall certainly go; but if you will not go with me, I shall not go.”

6608.label: Judges 4:9
6608.text: To this she said: “Without fail I shall go with you. Just the same, the beautifying thing will not become yours on the way that you are going, for it will be into the hand of a woman that Jehovah will sell Sisʹe·ra.” With that Debʹo·rah got up and went with Baʹrak to Keʹdesh.

6609.label: Judges 4:10
6609.text: And Baʹrak began to call Zebʹu·lun and Naphʹta·li together to Keʹdesh, and ten thousand men went on up following his steps; and Debʹo·rah went on up with him.

6610.label: Judges 4:11
6610.text: Incidentally Heʹber the Kenʹite had separated from the Kenʹites, the sons of Hoʹbab, whose son-in-law Moses was, and he had his tent pitched near the big tree in Za·a·nanʹnim, which is at Keʹdesh.

6611.label: Judges 4:12
6611.text: Then they reported to Sisʹe·ra that Baʹrak the son of A·binʹo·am had gone up to Mount Taʹbor.

6612.label: Judges 4:13
6612.text: At once Sisʹe·ra called together all his war chariots, the nine hundred war chariots with iron scythes, and all the people that were with him, out of Ha·roʹsheth of the nations to the torrent valley of Kiʹshon.

6613.label: Judges 4:14
6613.text: Debʹo·rah now said to Baʹrak: “Get up, for this is the day that Jehovah will certainly give Sisʹe·ra into your hand. Is it not Jehovah that has gone out before you?” And Baʹrak went descending from Mount Taʹbor with ten thousand men behind him.

6614.label: Judges 4:15
6614.text: And Jehovah began to throw Sisʹe·ra and all his war chariots and all the camp into confusion by the edge of the sword before Baʹrak. Finally Sisʹe·ra got down off the chariot and took to flight on foot.

6615.label: Judges 4:16
6615.text: And Baʹrak chased after the war chariots and the camp as far as Ha·roʹsheth of the nations, so that all the camp of Sisʹe·ra fell by the edge of the sword. Not as much as one remained.

6616.label: Judges 4:17
6616.text: As for Sisʹe·ra, he fled on foot to the tent of Jaʹel the wife of Heʹber the Kenʹite, for there was peace between Jaʹbin the king of Haʹzor and the household of Heʹber the Kenʹite.

6617.label: Judges 4:18
6617.text: Then Jaʹel came on out to meet Sisʹe·ra and said to him: “Turn this way, my lord, turn this way to me. Do not be afraid.” So he turned aside to her into the tent. Later she covered him with a blanket.

6618.label: Judges 4:19
6618.text: In time he said to her: “Give me, please, a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” Accordingly she opened a skin bottle of milk and gave him a drink, after which she covered him.

6619.label: Judges 4:20
6619.text: And he went on to say to her: “Stand at the entrance of the tent, and it must occur that if anybody comes and does ask you and says, ‘Is there a man here?’ you must then say, ‘No!’”

6620.label: Judges 4:21
6620.text: And Jaʹel the wife of Heʹber proceeded to take a pin of the tent and to put the hammer into her hand. Then she went to him stealthily and drove the pin into his temples and beat it into the earth, while he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.

6621.label: Judges 4:22
6621.text: And, look! there was Baʹrak pursuing Sisʹe·ra. Jaʹel now came on out to meet him and said to him: “Come and I shall show you the man you are looking for.” So in he went to her, and, look! there was Sisʹe·ra fallen dead, with the pin in his temples.

6622.label: Judges 4:23
6622.text: Thus God subdued Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan before the sons of Israel on that day.

6623.label: Judges 4:24
6623.text: And the hand of the sons of Israel went on getting harder and harder against Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan, until they had cut off Jaʹbin the king of Caʹnaan.

6624.label: Judges 5:1
6624.text: And on that day Debʹo·rah along with Baʹrak the son of A·binʹo·am broke out in song, saying:

6625.label: Judges 5:2
6625.text: “For letting the hair hang loose in Israel [for war],For the people’s volunteering, BLESS Jehovah.

6626.label: Judges 5:3
6626.text: Listen, YOU kings; give ear, YOU high officials:I to Jehovah, yes, I, will sing.I shall make melody to Jehovah, Israel’s God.

6627.label: Judges 5:4
6627.text: Jehovah, at your going forth from Seʹir, At your marching out of the field of Eʹdom, Earth rocked, heavens also dripped, Clouds also dripped with water.

6628.label: Judges 5:5
6628.text: Mountains flowed away from the face of Jehovah, This Siʹnai away from the face of Jehovah, Israel’s God.

6629.label: Judges 5:6
6629.text: In the days of Shamʹgar the son of Aʹnath,In the days of Jaʹel, pathways had no traffic, And the travelers of roadways would travel by roundabout pathways.

6630.label: Judges 5:7
6630.text: The dwellers in open country ceased, in Israel they ceased, Until I, Debʹo·rah, rose up,Until I rose up as a mother in Israel.

6631.label: Judges 5:8
6631.text: They proceeded to choose new gods. It was then there was war in the gates. A shield could not be seen, nor a lance,Among forty thousand in Israel.

6632.label: Judges 5:9
6632.text: My heart is for the commanders of Israel, Who were volunteers among the people. BLESS Jehovah.

6633.label: Judges 5:10
6633.text: YOU riders on yellowish-red she-asses, YOU who sit on rich carpets, And YOU who walk on the road,Consider!

6634.label: Judges 5:11
6634.text: Some of the voices of the water distributors among the places of drawing water, There they began to recount the righteous acts of Jehovah, The righteous acts of his dwellers in open country in Israel.It was then Jehovah’s people made their way down to the gates.

6635.label: Judges 5:12
6635.text: Awake, awake, O Debʹo·rah; Awake, awake, utter a song! Rise up, Baʹrak, and lead your captives away, you son of A·binʹo·am!

6636.label: Judges 5:13
6636.text: It was then the survivors came down to the majestic ones;Jehovah’s people came down to me against the mighty ones.

6637.label: Judges 5:14
6637.text: Out of Eʹphra·im was their origin in the low plain, With you, O Benjamin, among your peoples.Out of Maʹchir the commanders went down,And out of Zebʹu·lun those handling the equipment of a scribe.

6638.label: Judges 5:15
6638.text: And the princes in Isʹsa·char were with Debʹo·rah,And as Isʹsa·char, so was Baʹrak. Into the low plain he was sent on foot. Among the divisions of Reuʹben great were the searchings of the heart.

6639.label: Judges 5:16
6639.text: Why did you sit down between the two saddlebags,To listen to the pipings for the flocks? For the divisions of Reuʹben there were great searchings of the heart.

6640.label: Judges 5:17
6640.text: Gilʹe·ad kept to his residence on the other side of the Jordan; And Dan, why did he continue to dwell for the time in ships? Ashʹer sat idle at the seashore,And by his landing places he kept residing.

6641.label: Judges 5:18
6641.text: Zebʹu·lun was a people that scorned their souls to the point of death; Naphʹta·li also, on the heights of the field.

6642.label: Judges 5:19
6642.text: Kings came, they fought;It was then that the kings of Caʹnaan fought In Taʹa·nach by the waters of Me·gidʹdo. No gain of silver did they take.

6643.label: Judges 5:20
6643.text: From heaven did the stars fight, From their orbits they fought against Sisʹe·ra.

6644.label: Judges 5:21
6644.text: The torrent of Kiʹshon washed them away, The torrent of ancient days, the torrent of Kiʹshon. You went treading down strength, O my soul.

6645.label: Judges 5:22
6645.text: It was then that the hoofs of horses pawed Because of dashings upon dashings of his stallions.

6646.label: Judges 5:23
6646.text: ‘CURSE Meʹroz,’ said the angel of Jehovah, ‘CURSE its inhabitants incessantly,For they did not come to the assistance of Jehovah,To the assistance of Jehovah with the mighty ones.’

6647.label: Judges 5:24
6647.text: Jaʹel the wife of Heʹber the Kenʹite will be most blessed among women,Among women in the tent she will be most blessed.

6648.label: Judges 5:25
6648.text: Water he asked, milk she gave;In the large banquet bowl of majestic ones she presented curdled milk.

6649.label: Judges 5:26
6649.text: Her hand to the tent pin she then thrust out,And her right hand to the mallet of hard workers. And she hammered Sisʹe·ra, she pierced his head through, And she broke apart and cut up his temples.

6650.label: Judges 5:27
6650.text: Between her feet he collapsed, he fell, he lay down;Between her feet he collapsed, he fell;Where he collapsed, there he fell overcome.

6651.label: Judges 5:28
6651.text: From the window a woman looked out and kept watching for him, The mother of Sisʹe·ra from the lattice, ‘Why has his war chariot delayed in coming? Why must the hoofbeats of his chariots be so late?’

6652.label: Judges 5:29
6652.text: The wise ones of her noble ladies would answer her,Yes, she too would talk back to herself with her own sayings,

6653.label: Judges 5:30
6653.text: ‘Ought they not to find, ought they not to distribute spoil, A womb—two wombs to every able-bodied man, Spoil of dyed stuffs for Sisʹe·ra, spoil of dyed stuffs,An embroidered garment, dyed stuff, two embroidered garmentsFor the necks of [men of] spoil?’

6654.label: Judges 5:31
6654.text: Thus let all your enemies perish, O Jehovah,And let your lovers be as when the sun goes forth in its mightiness.” And the land had no further disturbance for forty years.

6655.label: Judges 6:1
6655.text: Then the sons of Israel began to do what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah. So Jehovah gave them into the hand of Midʹi·an for seven years.

6656.label: Judges 6:2
6656.text: And the hand of Midʹi·an came to prevail over Israel. Due to Midʹi·an the sons of Israel made for themselves the underground store places that were in the mountains, and the caves and the places difficult to approach.

6657.label: Judges 6:3
6657.text: And it occurred that, if Israel sowed seed, Midʹi·an and Amʹa·lek and the Easterners came up, yes, they came up against them.

6658.label: Judges 6:4
6658.text: And they would camp against them and would ruin the yield of the earth all the way to Gaʹza, and they would not let any sustenance or sheep or bull or ass remain in Israel.

6659.label: Judges 6:5
6659.text: For they and their livestock would come up with their tents. They would come as numerous as the locusts, and they and their camels were without number; and they would come into the land to ruin it.

6660.label: Judges 6:6
6660.text: And Israel became greatly impoverished due to Midʹi·an; and the sons of Israel began to call to Jehovah for aid.

6661.label: Judges 6:7
6661.text: And it came about that because the sons of Israel called to Jehovah for aid on account of Midʹi·an,

6662.label: Judges 6:8
6662.text: Jehovah proceeded to send a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel and to say to them: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘It was I who brought YOU up from Egypt and thus brought YOU out of the house of slaves.

6663.label: Judges 6:9
6663.text: So I delivered YOU out of the hand of Egypt and out of the hand of all YOUR oppressors and drove them out from before YOU and gave YOU their land.

6664.label: Judges 6:10
6664.text: Furthermore, I said to YOU: “I am Jehovah YOUR God. YOU must not fear the gods of the Amʹor·ites in whose land YOU are dwelling.” And YOU did not listen to my voice.’”

6665.label: Judges 6:11
6665.text: Later Jehovah’s angel came and sat under the big tree that was in Ophʹrah, which belonged to Joʹash the Abi-ezʹrite, while Gidʹe·on his son was beating out wheat in the winepress so as to get it quickly out of the sight of Midʹi·an.

6666.label: Judges 6:12
6666.text: Then Jehovah’s angel appeared to him and said to him: “Jehovah is with you, you valiant, mighty one.”

6667.label: Judges 6:13
6667.text: At this Gidʹe·on said to him: “Excuse me, my lord, but if Jehovah is with us, then why has all this come upon us, and where are all his wonderful acts that our fathers related to us, saying, ‘Was it not out of Egypt that Jehovah brought us up?’ And now Jehovah has deserted us, and he gives us into the palm of Midʹi·an.”

6668.label: Judges 6:14
6668.text: Upon that Jehovah faced him and said: “Go in this power of yours, and you will certainly save Israel out of Midʹi·an’s palm. Do I not send you?”

6669.label: Judges 6:15
6669.text: In turn he said to him: “Excuse me, Jehovah. With what shall I save Israel? Look! My thousand is the least in Ma·nasʹseh, and I am the smallest in my father’s house.”

6670.label: Judges 6:16
6670.text: But Jehovah said to him: “Because I shall prove to be with you, and you will certainly strike down Midʹi·an as if one man.”

6671.label: Judges 6:17
6671.text: At this he said to him: “If, now, I have found favor in your eyes, you must also perform a sign for me that you are the one speaking with me.

6672.label: Judges 6:18
6672.text: Do not, please, move away from here until I come to you and I have brought out my gift and set it before you.” Accordingly he said: “I, for my part, shall keep sitting here until you return.”

6673.label: Judges 6:19
6673.text: And Gidʹe·on went in and proceeded to make ready a kid of the goats and an eʹphah of flour as unfermented cakes. The meat he put in the basket, and the broth he put in the cooking pot, after which he brought it out to him under the big tree and served it.

6674.label: Judges 6:20
6674.text: The angel of the [true] God now said to him: “Take the meat and the unfermented cakes and set them on the big rock there, and pour out the broth.” At that he did so.

6675.label: Judges 6:21
6675.text: Then Jehovah’s angel thrust out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unfermented cakes, and fire began to ascend out of the rock and to consume the meat and the unfermented cakes. As for Jehovah’s angel, he vanished from his sight.

6676.label: Judges 6:22
6676.text: Consequently Gidʹe·on realized that it was Jehovah’s angel. At once Gidʹe·on said: “Alas, Sovereign Lord Jehovah, for the reason that I have seen Jehovah’s angel face to face!”

6677.label: Judges 6:23
6677.text: But Jehovah said to him: “Peace be yours. Do not fear. You will not die.”

6678.label: Judges 6:24
6678.text: So Gidʹe·on built an altar there to Jehovah, and it continues to be called Je·hoʹvah-shaʹlom down to this day. It is yet in Ophʹrah of the Abi-ezʹrites.

6679.label: Judges 6:25
6679.text: And it came about during that night that Jehovah went on to say to him: “Take the young bull, the bull that belongs to your father, that is, the second young bull of seven years, and you must tear down the altar of Baʹal that is your father’s, and the sacred pole that is by it you should cut down.

6680.label: Judges 6:26
6680.text: And you must build an altar to Jehovah your God at the head of this stronghold, with the row of stones, and you must take the second young bull and offer it up as a burnt offering on the pieces of wood of the sacred pole that you will cut down.”

6681.label: Judges 6:27
6681.text: Accordingly Gidʹe·on took ten men of his servants and went doing just as Jehovah had spoken to him; but it came about that, as he feared the household of his father and the men of the city too much to do it by day, he went doing it by night.

6682.label: Judges 6:28
6682.text: When the men of the city got up early in the morning as usual, why, look! the altar of Baʹal had been pulled down and the sacred pole that was beside it had been cut down, and the second young bull had been offered up on the altar that had been built.

6683.label: Judges 6:29
6683.text: And they began to say one to another: “Who has done this thing?” And they went inquiring and seeking. Finally they said: “Gidʹe·on the son of Joʹash is the one that has done this thing.”

6684.label: Judges 6:30
6684.text: So the men of the city said to Joʹash: “Bring your son out that he may die, because he has pulled down the altar of Baʹal, and because he has cut down the sacred pole that was by it.”

6685.label: Judges 6:31
6685.text: At this Joʹash said to all those who stood against him: “Will YOU be the ones to make a legal defense for Baʹal to see whether YOU yourselves may save him? Whoever makes a legal defense for him ought to be put to death even this morning. If he is God, let him make a legal defense for himself, because someone has pulled down his altar.”

6686.label: Judges 6:32
6686.text: And he began to call him Jer·ub·baʹal on that day, saying: “Let Baʹal make a legal defense in his own behalf, because someone has pulled down his altar.”

6687.label: Judges 6:33
6687.text: And all Midʹi·an and Amʹa·lek and the Easterners gathered together as one and proceeded to cross over and camp in the low plain of Jezʹre·el.

6688.label: Judges 6:34
6688.text: And Jehovah’s spirit enveloped Gidʹe·on so that he went blowing the horn, and the Abi-ezʹrites got to be called together after him.

6689.label: Judges 6:35
6689.text: And he sent out messengers through all of Ma·nasʹseh, and they too got to be called together after him. He also sent out messengers through Ashʹer and Zebʹu·lun and Naphʹta·li, and they came on up to meet him.

6690.label: Judges 6:36
6690.text: Then Gidʹe·on said to the [true] God: “If you are saving Israel by means of me, just as you have promised,

6691.label: Judges 6:37
6691.text: here I am keeping a fleece of wool exposed on the threshing floor. If dew comes to be on the fleece alone but on all the earth there is dryness, then I must know that you will save Israel by means of me, just as you have promised.”

6692.label: Judges 6:38
6692.text: And it turned out to be that way. When he rose up early the next day and wrung the fleece, he got to drain off enough dew from the fleece to fill a large banquet bowl with water.

6693.label: Judges 6:39
6693.text: However, Gidʹe·on said to the [true] God: “Do not let your anger blaze against me, but let me speak just once more. Let me, please, make a test only once more with the fleece. Let, please, dryness occur to the fleece alone, and upon all the earth let there come to be dew.”

6694.label: Judges 6:40
6694.text: So God did that way on that night; and dryness came to be on the fleece alone, and upon all the earth dew occurred.

6695.label: Judges 7:1
6695.text: Then Jer·ub·baʹal, that is to say, Gidʹe·on, and all the people who were with him, rose early and took up camping at the well of Haʹrod; and the camp of Midʹi·an happened to be on the north of him, at the hill of Moʹreh, in the low plain.

6696.label: Judges 7:2
6696.text: Jehovah now said to Gidʹe·on: “The people who are with you are too many for me to give Midʹi·an into their hand. Perhaps Israel would brag about itself against me, saying, ‘My hand it was that saved me.’

6697.label: Judges 7:3
6697.text: And now call out, please, in the hearing of the people, saying, ‘Who is there afraid and trembling? Let him retire.’” So Gidʹe·on put them to the proof. With that, twenty-two thousand of the people retired, and there were ten thousand that remained.

6698.label: Judges 7:4
6698.text: Still Jehovah said to Gidʹe·on: “There are yet too many people. Have them go down to the water that I may put them to the proof for you there. And it must occur that of whomever I say to you, ‘This one will go with you,’ he is one that will go with you, but every one of whom I say to you, ‘This one will not go along with you,’ he is one that will not go along.”

6699.label: Judges 7:5
6699.text: So he had the people go down to the water. Then Jehovah said to Gidʹe·on: “Every one that laps up some of the water with his tongue just as a dog laps, you will set him by himself, also every one that bends down upon his knees to drink.”

6700.label: Judges 7:6
6700.text: And the number of those lapping with their hand to their mouth turned out to be three hundred men. As for all the rest of the people, they bent down upon their knees to drink water.

6701.label: Judges 7:7
6701.text: Jehovah now said to Gidʹe·on: “By the three hundred men who did the lapping I shall save YOU people, and I will give Midʹi·an into your hand. As for all the other people, let them go each one to his place.”

6702.label: Judges 7:8
6702.text: So they took the provisions of the people in their hand, and their horns, and all the men of Israel he sent away each one to his home; and he kept hold of the three hundred men. As for the camp of Midʹi·an, it happened to be down below him in the low plain.

6703.label: Judges 7:9
6703.text: And it came about during that night that Jehovah proceeded to say to him: “Rise up, descend upon the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

6704.label: Judges 7:10
6704.text: But if you are afraid to descend, descend, you with Puʹrah your attendant, to the camp.

6705.label: Judges 7:11
6705.text: And you must listen to what they will speak, and afterward your hands will certainly grow strong, and you will be certain to descend upon the camp.” At that he and Puʹrah his attendant made their descent to the edge of those in battle formation who were in the camp.

6706.label: Judges 7:12
6706.text: Now Midʹi·an and Amʹa·lek and all the Easterners were plumped in the low plain as numerous as locusts; and their camels were without number, as numerous as the grains of sand that are on the seashore.

6707.label: Judges 7:13
6707.text: Gidʹe·on now came, and, look! there was a man relating a dream to his companion, and he went on to say: “Here is a dream that I have dreamed. And, look! there was a round cake of barley bread turning over and over into the camp of Midʹi·an. Then it came to a tent and struck it so that it fell, and it went turning it upside down, and the tent fell flat.”

6708.label: Judges 7:14
6708.text: At this his companion answered and said: “This is nothing else but the sword of Gidʹe·on the son of Joʹash, a man of Israel. The [true] God has given Midʹi·an and all the camp into his hand.”

6709.label: Judges 7:15
6709.text: And it came about that as soon as Gidʹe·on heard the relating of the dream and its explanation, he began to worship. After that he returned to the camp of Israel and said: “Get up, for Jehovah has given the camp of Midʹi·an into YOUR hand.”

6710.label: Judges 7:16
6710.text: Then he divided the three hundred men up into three bands and put horns in the hands of all of them and large empty jars, and torches inside the large jars.

6711.label: Judges 7:17
6711.text: And he went on to say to them: “YOU should learn from watching me, and that is how YOU should do. And when I am come to the edge of the camp, it must also occur that just as I shall do, so YOU will do.

6712.label: Judges 7:18
6712.text: When I have blown the horn, I and all who are with me, YOU also must blow the horns, YOU too, round about all the camp, and YOU must say, ‘Jehovah’s and Gidʹe·on’s!’”

6713.label: Judges 7:19
6713.text: In time Gidʹe·on came with the hundred men who were with him to the edge of the camp at the start of the middle night watch. They had just got through posting the sentries. And they proceeded to blow the horns, and there was a dashing to pieces of the large water jars that were in their hands.

6714.label: Judges 7:20
6714.text: At that the three bands blew the horns and shattered the large jars and took fresh hold on the torches with their left hand and with their right hand on the horns to blow them, and they began calling out: “Jehovah’s sword and Gidʹe·on’s!”

6715.label: Judges 7:21
6715.text: All the while they kept standing each one in his place all around the camp, and the whole camp got on the run and broke out into shouting and went fleeing.

6716.label: Judges 7:22
6716.text: And the three hundred continued to blow the horns, and Jehovah proceeded to set the sword of each one against the other in all the camp; and the camp kept up their flight as far as Beth-shitʹtah, on to Zerʹe·rah, as far as the outskirts of Aʹbel-me·hoʹlah by Tabʹbath.

6717.label: Judges 7:23
6717.text: Meantime the men of Israel were called together from Naphʹta·li and Ashʹer and all of Ma·nasʹseh, and they went chasing after Midʹi·an.

6718.label: Judges 7:24
6718.text: And Gidʹe·on sent messengers into all the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im, saying: “Go down to meet Midʹi·an and capture ahead of them the waters as far as Beth-barʹah and the Jordan.” So all the men of Eʹphra·im were called together, and they got to capture the waters as far as Beth-barʹah and the Jordan.

6719.label: Judges 7:25
6719.text: They also got to capture the two princes of Midʹi·an, namely, Oʹreb and Zeʹeb; and they proceeded to kill Oʹreb on the rock of Oʹreb, and they killed Zeʹeb at the wine vat of Zeʹeb. And they kept on pursuing Midʹi·an, and they brought the head of Oʹreb and that of Zeʹeb to Gidʹe·on in the region of the Jordan.

6720.label: Judges 8:1
6720.text: Then the men of Eʹphra·im said to him: “What sort of thing is this that you have done to us in not calling us when you went to fight against Midʹi·an?” And they vehemently tried to pick a quarrel with him.

6721.label: Judges 8:2
6721.text: Finally he said to them: “What now have I done in comparison with YOU? Are not the gleanings of Eʹphra·im better than the grape gathering of Abi-eʹzer?

6722.label: Judges 8:3
6722.text: It was into YOUR hand that God gave Midʹi·an’s princes Oʹreb and Zeʹeb, and what have I been able to do in comparison with YOU?” It was then that their spirit calmed down toward him when he spoke this word.

6723.label: Judges 8:4
6723.text: Eventually Gidʹe·on came to the Jordan, crossing it, he and the three hundred men that were with him, tired but keeping up the pursuit.

6724.label: Judges 8:5
6724.text: Later he said to the men of Sucʹcoth: “Please give round loaves of bread to the people that are following my steps, for they are tired and I am chasing after Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna, the kings of Midʹi·an.”

6725.label: Judges 8:6
6725.text: But the princes of Sucʹcoth said: “Are the palms of Zeʹbah and of Zal·munʹna already in your hand so that bread has to be given to your army?”

6726.label: Judges 8:7
6726.text: At this Gidʹe·on said: “That is why when Jehovah gives Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna into my hand, I shall certainly give YOUR flesh a threshing with the thorns of the wilderness and the briers.”

6727.label: Judges 8:8
6727.text: And he continued on his way up from there to Pe·nuʹel and went speaking to them in this same manner, but the men of Pe·nuʹel answered him just as the men of Sucʹcoth had answered.

6728.label: Judges 8:9
6728.text: Hence he said also to the men of Pe·nuʹel: “When I return in peace, I shall pull down this tower.”

6729.label: Judges 8:10
6729.text: Now Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna were in Karʹkor, and their camps with them, about fifteen thousand being all who were left over out of the entire camp of the Easterners; and those already fallen were a hundred and twenty thousand men who used to draw the sword.

6730.label: Judges 8:11
6730.text: And Gidʹe·on continued on up by the way of those residing in tents to the east of Noʹbah and Jogʹbe·hah and began to strike the camp while the camp happened to be off guard.

6731.label: Judges 8:12
6731.text: When Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna took to flight, he at once went in pursuit of them and got to capture Midʹi·an’s two kings, Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna; and he drove all the camp into trembling.

6732.label: Judges 8:13
6732.text: And Gidʹe·on the son of Joʹash began his return from the war by the pass that goes up to Heʹres.

6733.label: Judges 8:14
6733.text: En route he captured a young man of the men of Sucʹcoth and made inquiries of him. So he wrote out for him the names of the princes of Sucʹcoth and its older men, seventy-seven men.

6734.label: Judges 8:15
6734.text: With that he went to the men of Sucʹcoth and said: “Here are Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna respecting whom YOU taunted me, saying, ‘Are the palms of Zeʹbah and of Zal·munʹna already in your hand so that bread has to be given to your tired-out men?’”

6735.label: Judges 8:16
6735.text: Then he took the older men of the city and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he put the men of Sucʹcoth through an experience.

6736.label: Judges 8:17
6736.text: And the tower of Pe·nuʹel he pulled down, and he proceeded to kill the men of the city.

6737.label: Judges 8:18
6737.text: He now said to Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna: “What sort of men were they whom YOU killed in Taʹbor?” To this they said: “As you are, so were they, each one, like the sons of a king in form.”

6738.label: Judges 8:19
6738.text: At that he said: “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As Jehovah lives, if YOU had preserved them alive, I would not have to kill YOU.”

6739.label: Judges 8:20
6739.text: Then he said to Jeʹther his firstborn: “Get up, kill them.” And the young man did not draw his sword, because he was afraid, for he was yet a young man.

6740.label: Judges 8:21
6740.text: So Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna said: “Get up yourself and assault us, for as a man is, so is his mightiness.” Accordingly Gidʹe·on got up and killed Zeʹbah and Zal·munʹna and took the moon-shaped ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.

6741.label: Judges 8:22
6741.text: Later the men of Israel said to Gidʹe·on: “Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson as well, for you have saved us out of the hand of Midʹi·an.”

6742.label: Judges 8:23
6742.text: But Gidʹe·on said to them: “I myself shall not rule over YOU, nor will my son rule over YOU. Jehovah is the one who will rule over YOU.”

6743.label: Judges 8:24
6743.text: And Gidʹe·on went on to say to them: “Let me make a request of YOU: Give me, each one of YOU, the nose ring of his booty.” (For they had nose rings of gold, because they were Ishʹma·el·ites.)

6744.label: Judges 8:25
6744.text: Then they said: “We shall surely give them.” With that they spread out a mantle and went throwing each one the nose ring of his booty into it.

6745.label: Judges 8:26
6745.text: And the weight of the nose rings of gold that he had requested amounted to one thousand seven hundred gold shekels, besides the moon-shaped ornaments and the eardrops and the garments of wool dyed reddish purple that were upon the kings of Midʹi·an and besides the necklaces that were on the necks of the camels.

6746.label: Judges 8:27
6746.text: And Gidʹe·on proceeded to make it into an ephʹod and to exhibit it in his city Ophʹrah; and all Israel began to have immoral intercourse with it there, so that it served as a snare to Gidʹe·on and to his household.

6747.label: Judges 8:28
6747.text: Thus Midʹi·an was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not lift up their head anymore; and the land had no further disturbance for forty years in the days of Gidʹe·on.

6748.label: Judges 8:29
6748.text: And Jer·ub·baʹal the son of Joʹash went his way and continued to dwell in his house.

6749.label: Judges 8:30
6749.text: And Gidʹe·on came to have seventy sons that issued out of his upper thigh, for he came to have many wives.

6750.label: Judges 8:31
6750.text: As for the concubine of his that was in Sheʹchem, she too bore him a son. So he named him A·bimʹe·lech.

6751.label: Judges 8:32
6751.text: Eventually Gidʹe·on the son of Joʹash died at a good old age and was buried in the burial place of Joʹash his father in Ophʹrah of the Abi-ezʹrites.

6752.label: Judges 8:33
6752.text: And it came about that as soon as Gidʹe·on had died the sons of Israel again took up having immoral intercourse with the Baʹals, so that they appointed Baʹal-beʹrith as their god.

6753.label: Judges 8:34
6753.text: And the sons of Israel did not remember Jehovah their God, who had delivered them out of the hand of all their enemies round about;

6754.label: Judges 8:35
6754.text: and they did not exercise loving-kindness toward the household of Jer·ub·baʹal, Gidʹe·on, in return for all the goodness that he had exercised toward Israel.

6755.label: Judges 9:1
6755.text: In time A·bimʹe·lech the son of Jer·ub·baʹal went to Sheʹchem to the brothers of his mother and began speaking to them and to all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying:

6756.label: Judges 9:2
6756.text: “Speak, please, in the hearing of all the landowners of Sheʹchem, ‘Which is better for YOU, for seventy men, all the sons of Jer·ub·baʹal, to rule over YOU or for one man to rule over YOU? And YOU must remember that YOUR bone and YOUR flesh I am.’”

6757.label: Judges 9:3
6757.text: So the brothers of his mother began speaking all these words about him in the hearing of all the landowners of Sheʹchem so that their heart inclined toward A·bimʹe·lech, for they said: “He is our own brother.”

6758.label: Judges 9:4
6758.text: Then they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baʹal-beʹrith, and with them A·bimʹe·lech proceeded to hire idle and insolent men, that they might accompany him.

6759.label: Judges 9:5
6759.text: After that he went to the house of his father at Ophʹrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jer·ub·baʹal, seventy men, upon one stone, but Joʹtham the youngest son of Jer·ub·baʹal was left over, because he had hid.

6760.label: Judges 9:6
6760.text: Subsequently all the landowners of Sheʹchem and all the house of Milʹlo gathered together and went and made A·bimʹe·lech reign as king, close by the big tree, the pillar that was in Sheʹchem.

6761.label: Judges 9:7
6761.text: When they reported it to Joʹtham he at once went and stood on the top of Mount Gerʹi·zim and raised his voice and called out and said to them: “Listen to me, YOU landowners of Sheʹchem, and let God listen to YOU:

6762.label: Judges 9:8
6762.text: “Once upon a time the trees went to anoint a king over them. So they said to the olive tree, ‘Do be king over us.’

6763.label: Judges 9:9
6763.text: But the olive tree said to them, ‘Must I give up my fatness with which they glorify God and men, and must I go to wave over the other trees?’

6764.label: Judges 9:10
6764.text: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You come, be queen over us.’

6765.label: Judges 9:11
6765.text: But the fig tree said to them, ‘Must I give up my sweetness and my good produce, and must I go to wave over the other trees?’

6766.label: Judges 9:12
6766.text: Next the trees said to the vine, ‘You come, be queen over us.’

6767.label: Judges 9:13
6767.text: In turn the vine said to them, ‘Must I give up my new wine that makes God and men rejoice, and must I go to wave over the trees?’

6768.label: Judges 9:14
6768.text: Finally all the other trees said to the bramble, ‘You come, be king over us.’

6769.label: Judges 9:15
6769.text: At this the bramble said to the trees, ‘If it is in truth that YOU are anointing me as king over YOU, come, seek refuge under my shadow. But if not, let fire come out of the bramble and consume the cedars of Lebʹa·non.’

6770.label: Judges 9:16
6770.text: “And now if it is in truth and in faultlessness that YOU have acted and that YOU went making A·bimʹe·lech king, and if it is goodness that YOU have exercised toward Jer·ub·baʹal and his household, and if YOU have done to him as the doing of his hands deserved,

6771.label: Judges 9:17
6771.text: when my father fought for YOU and went risking his soul that he might deliver YOU out of Midʹi·an’s hand;

6772.label: Judges 9:18
6772.text: and YOU, for YOUR part, have risen up against the household of my father today that YOU might kill his sons, seventy men, upon one stone, and that YOU might make A·bimʹe·lech, the son of his slave girl, king over the landowners of Sheʹchem just because he is YOUR own brother;

6773.label: Judges 9:19
6773.text: yes, if it is in truth and in faultlessness that YOU have acted toward Jer·ub·baʹal and his household this day, rejoice over A·bimʹe·lech and let him too rejoice over YOU.

6774.label: Judges 9:20
6774.text: But if not, let fire come out of A·bimʹe·lech and consume the landowners of Sheʹchem and the house of Milʹlo, and let fire come out of the landowners of Sheʹchem and the house of Milʹlo and consume A·bimʹe·lech.”

6775.label: Judges 9:21
6775.text: Then Joʹtham took to flight and went running off and made his way to Beʹer, and he took up dwelling there because of A·bimʹe·lech his brother.

6776.label: Judges 9:22
6776.text: And A·bimʹe·lech kept playing the prince over Israel three years.

6777.label: Judges 9:23
6777.text: Then God let develop a bad spirit between A·bimʹe·lech and the landowners of Sheʹchem, and the landowners of Sheʹchem proceeded to deal treacherously with A·bimʹe·lech,

6778.label: Judges 9:24
6778.text: that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jer·ub·baʹal might come and that he might put their blood upon A·bimʹe·lech their brother because he killed them, and upon the landowners of Sheʹchem because they strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.

6779.label: Judges 9:25
6779.text: So the landowners of Sheʹchem set ambush men for him upon the tops of the mountains, and they would rob everyone that would pass by them on the road. In time it was reported to A·bimʹe·lech.

6780.label: Judges 9:26
6780.text: Then Gaʹal the son of Eʹbed and his brothers came and crossed over into Sheʹchem, and the landowners of Sheʹchem began to trust in him.

6781.label: Judges 9:27
6781.text: And they went out as usual into the field and engaged in gathering the grapes of their vineyards and in treading them and in carrying on a festal exultation, after which they went into the house of their god and ate and drank and called down evil upon A·bimʹe·lech.

6782.label: Judges 9:28
6782.text: And Gaʹal the son of Eʹbed went on to say: “Who is A·bimʹe·lech, and who is Sheʹchem that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jer·ub·baʹal, and is not Zeʹbul a commissioner of his? Serve the men of Haʹmor, Sheʹchem’s father, YOU others, but why should we ourselves serve him?

6783.label: Judges 9:29
6783.text: And if only this people were in my hand! Then I would remove A·bimʹe·lech.” And he went on to say to A·bimʹe·lech: “Make your army numerous and come on out.”

6784.label: Judges 9:30
6784.text: And Zeʹbul the prince of the city got to hear the words of Gaʹal the son of Eʹbed. Then his anger blazed.

6785.label: Judges 9:31
6785.text: So he sent messengers by subterfuge to A·bimʹe·lech, saying: “Look! Gaʹal the son of Eʹbed and his brothers are now come to Sheʹchem, and here they are massing the city against you.

6786.label: Judges 9:32
6786.text: And now rise up by night, you and the people that are with you, and lie in wait in the field.

6787.label: Judges 9:33
6787.text: And it must occur in the morning that as soon as the sun shines forth you should get up early, and you must make a dash against the city; and when he and the people that are with him are going out against you, you must also do to him just as your hand finds it possible.”

6788.label: Judges 9:34
6788.text: Accordingly A·bimʹe·lech and all the people that were with him rose up by night, and they began to lie in wait against Sheʹchem in four bands.

6789.label: Judges 9:35
6789.text: Later Gaʹal the son of Eʹbed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate. Then A·bimʹe·lech and the people that were with him rose up from the place of ambush.

6790.label: Judges 9:36
6790.text: When Gaʹal caught sight of the people, he at once said to Zeʹbul: “Look! People coming down from the tops of the mountains.” But Zeʹbul said to him: “The shadows of the mountains are what you are seeing as though they were men.”

6791.label: Judges 9:37
6791.text: Later Gaʹal spoke once more and said: “Look! People coming down out of the center of the land, and one band is coming by the way of the big tree of Me·onʹe·nim.”

6792.label: Judges 9:38
6792.text: At this Zeʹbul said to him: “Where now is that saying of yours that you mouthed, ‘Who is A·bimʹe·lech that we should serve him?’ Is not this the people whom you rejected? Go out now, please, and fight against them.”

6793.label: Judges 9:39
6793.text: So Gaʹal went on out at the head of the landowners of Sheʹchem and took up the fight against A·bimʹe·lech.

6794.label: Judges 9:40
6794.text: And A·bimʹe·lech set out after him, and he went fleeing before him; and the slain kept falling in numbers as far as the entrance of the gate.

6795.label: Judges 9:41
6795.text: And A·bimʹe·lech continued to dwell in A·ruʹmah, and Zeʹbul proceeded to drive Gaʹal and his brothers out from dwelling in Sheʹchem.

6796.label: Judges 9:42
6796.text: And it came about on the next day that the people began to go out into the field. So they told A·bimʹe·lech.

6797.label: Judges 9:43
6797.text: Hence he took the people and divided them up into three bands and began to lie in wait in the field. Then he looked, and there the people were going out of the city. He now rose up against them and struck them down.

6798.label: Judges 9:44
6798.text: And A·bimʹe·lech and the bands that were with him made a dash that they might stand at the entrance of the city gate, while two bands made a dash against all who were in the field, and they went striking them down.

6799.label: Judges 9:45
6799.text: And A·bimʹe·lech fought against the city all that day and got to capture the city; and he killed the people that were in it, after which he pulled the city down and sowed it with salt.

6800.label: Judges 9:46
6800.text: When all the landowners of the tower of Sheʹchem heard of it, they immediately went to the vault of the house of El-beʹrith.

6801.label: Judges 9:47
6801.text: Then it was reported to A·bimʹe·lech that all the landowners of the tower of Sheʹchem had collected together.

6802.label: Judges 9:48
6802.text: At that A·bimʹe·lech went up Mount Zalʹmon, he and all the people that were with him. A·bimʹe·lech now took an ax in his hand and cut down a branch of the trees and lifted it up and put it on his shoulder and said to the people that were with him: “What YOU have seen me do—hurry up, do like me!”

6803.label: Judges 9:49
6803.text: So all the people cut down also each one a branch for himself and went following A·bimʹe·lech. Then they put them against the vault, and over them they set the vault on fire, so that all the men of the tower of Sheʹchem died too, about a thousand men and women.

6804.label: Judges 9:50
6804.text: And A·bimʹe·lech proceeded to go to Theʹbez and to camp against Theʹbez and capture it.

6805.label: Judges 9:51
6805.text: As a strong tower happened to be in the middle of the city, there was where all the men and women and all the landowners of the city went fleeing, after which they shut it behind them and climbed onto the roof of the tower.

6806.label: Judges 9:52
6806.text: And A·bimʹe·lech made his way to the tower and began fighting against it, and he went on up close to the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.

6807.label: Judges 9:53
6807.text: Then a certain woman pitched an upper millstone upon A·bimʹe·lech’s head and broke his skull in pieces.

6808.label: Judges 9:54
6808.text: So he quickly called the attendant bearing his weapons and said to him: “Draw your sword and put me to death, for fear they should say about me, ‘It was a woman that killed him.’” Immediately his attendant ran him through, so that he died.

6809.label: Judges 9:55
6809.text: When the men of Israel got to see that A·bimʹe·lech had died, they now went each one to his place.

6810.label: Judges 9:56
6810.text: Thus God made the evil of A·bimʹe·lech that he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers come back.

6811.label: Judges 9:57
6811.text: And all the evil of the men of Sheʹchem God made come back upon their own heads, that the malediction of Joʹtham the son of Jer·ub·baʹal might come upon them.

6812.label: Judges 10:1
6812.text: Now after A·bimʹe·lech there rose up to save Israel Toʹla the son of Puʹah, the son of Doʹdo, a man of Isʹsa·char, and he was dwelling in Shaʹmir in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im.

6813.label: Judges 10:2
6813.text: And he continued to judge Israel for twenty-three years, after which he died and was buried in Shaʹmir.

6814.label: Judges 10:3
6814.text: Then after him Jaʹir the Gilʹe·ad·ite rose up, and he continued to judge Israel for twenty-two years.

6815.label: Judges 10:4
6815.text: And he came to have thirty sons who rode on thirty full-grown asses, and they had thirty cities. These they continue to call Havʹvoth-jaʹir down to this day; they are in the land of Gilʹe·ad.

6816.label: Judges 10:5
6816.text: After that Jaʹir died and was buried in Kaʹmon.

6817.label: Judges 10:6
6817.text: And the sons of Israel again proceeded to do what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah, and they began to serve the Baʹals and the Ashʹto·reth images and the gods of Syria and the gods of Siʹdon and the gods of Moʹab and the gods of the sons of Amʹmon and the gods of the Phi·lisʹtines. So they left Jehovah and did not serve him.

6818.label: Judges 10:7
6818.text: At this Jehovah’s anger blazed against Israel, so that he sold them into the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines and into the hand of the sons of Amʹmon.

6819.label: Judges 10:8
6819.text: Hence they shattered and heavily oppressed the sons of Israel in that year—for eighteen years all the sons of Israel that were on the side of the Jordan in the land of the Amʹor·ites that was in Gilʹe·ad.

6820.label: Judges 10:9
6820.text: And the sons of Amʹmon would cross the Jordan to fight even against Judah and Benjamin and the house of Eʹphra·im; and Israel was greatly distressed.

6821.label: Judges 10:10
6821.text: And the sons of Israel began to call to Jehovah for aid, saying: “We have sinned against you, because we have left our God and we serve the Baʹals.”

6822.label: Judges 10:11
6822.text: Then Jehovah said to the sons of Israel: “Was it not from Egypt and from the Amʹor·ites and from the sons of Amʹmon and from the Phi·lisʹtines

6823.label: Judges 10:12
6823.text: and the Si·doʹni·ans and Amʹa·lek and Midʹi·an, when they oppressed YOU and YOU went crying out to me, that I proceeded to save YOU out of their hand?

6824.label: Judges 10:13
6824.text: As for YOU, YOU abandoned me and took up serving other gods. That is why I shall not save YOU again.

6825.label: Judges 10:14
6825.text: Go and call for aid to the gods whom YOU have chosen. Let them be the ones to save YOU in the time of YOUR distress.”

6826.label: Judges 10:15
6826.text: But the sons of Israel said to Jehovah: “We have sinned. You yourself do to us according to anything that is good in your eyes. Only deliver us, please, this day.”

6827.label: Judges 10:16
6827.text: And they began to remove the foreign gods from their midst and to serve Jehovah, so that his soul became impatient because of the trouble of Israel.

6828.label: Judges 10:17
6828.text: In time the sons of Amʹmon were called together and pitched camp in Gilʹe·ad. So the sons of Israel gathered themselves together and pitched camp in Mizʹpah.

6829.label: Judges 10:18
6829.text: And the people and the princes of Gilʹe·ad began to say to one another: “Who is the man that will take the lead in fighting against the sons of Amʹmon? Let him become the head of all the inhabitants of Gilʹe·ad.”

6830.label: Judges 11:1
6830.text: Now Jephʹthah the Gilʹe·ad·ite had become a mighty, valiant man, and he was the son of a prostitute woman, and Gilʹe·ad came to be the father of Jephʹthah.

6831.label: Judges 11:2
6831.text: And Gilʹe·ad’s wife kept bearing sons to him. When the sons of the wife got big, they proceeded to drive Jephʹthah out and to say to him: “You must have no inheritance in the household of our father, for you are the son of another woman.”

6832.label: Judges 11:3
6832.text: So Jephʹthah ran away because of his brothers and took up dwelling in the land of Tob. And idle men kept bringing themselves together to Jephʹthah, and they would go out with him.

6833.label: Judges 11:4
6833.text: And it came about after a while that the sons of Amʹmon began to fight against Israel.

6834.label: Judges 11:5
6834.text: And it came about that when the sons of Amʹmon did fight against Israel, the older men of Gilʹe·ad immediately went to take Jephʹthah out of the land of Tob.

6835.label: Judges 11:6
6835.text: Then they said to Jephʹthah: “Do come and serve as our commander, and let us fight against the sons of Amʹmon.”

6836.label: Judges 11:7
6836.text: But Jephʹthah said to the older men of Gilʹe·ad: “Was it not YOU that hated me so that YOU drove me out of my father’s house? And why is it that YOU have come to me now just when YOU are in distress?”

6837.label: Judges 11:8
6837.text: At this the older men of Gilʹe·ad said to Jephʹthah: “That is why now we have returned to you, and you must go with us and fight against the sons of Amʹmon, and you must become for us the head of all the inhabitants of Gilʹe·ad.”

6838.label: Judges 11:9
6838.text: So Jephʹthah said to the older men of Gilʹe·ad: “If YOU are bringing me back to fight against the sons of Amʹmon, and Jehovah does abandon them to me, I, for my part, shall become YOUR head!”

6839.label: Judges 11:10
6839.text: In turn the older men of Gilʹe·ad said to Jephʹthah: “Let Jehovah prove to be the listener between us if the way we shall do is not according to your word.”

6840.label: Judges 11:11
6840.text: Consequently Jephʹthah went with the older men of Gilʹe·ad and the people set him over them as head and commander. And Jephʹthah proceeded to speak all his words before Jehovah in Mizʹpah.

6841.label: Judges 11:12
6841.text: Then Jephʹthah sent messengers to the king of the sons of Amʹmon, saying: “What do I have to do with you, seeing that you have come against me to fight in my land?”

6842.label: Judges 11:13
6842.text: So the king of the sons of Amʹmon said to the messengers of Jephʹthah: “It is because Israel took my land when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arʹnon as far as the Jabʹbok and as far as the Jordan. And now do return it peacefully.”

6843.label: Judges 11:14
6843.text: But Jephʹthah sent once more messengers to the king of the sons of Amʹmon

6844.label: Judges 11:15
6844.text: and said to him: “This is what Jephʹthah has said, ‘Israel did not take the land of Moʹab and the land of the sons of Amʹmon.

6845.label: Judges 11:16
6845.text: For when they came up out of Egypt Israel went walking through the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and got to come to Kaʹdesh.

6846.label: Judges 11:17
6846.text: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Eʹdom, saying: “Let me pass, please, through your land,” and the king of Eʹdom did not listen. And also to the king of Moʹab they sent, and he did not consent. And Israel kept dwelling in Kaʹdesh.

6847.label: Judges 11:18
6847.text: When they walked on through the wilderness, they went their way around the land of Eʹdom and the land of Moʹab, so that they went toward the rising of the sun as respects the land of Moʹab and took up camping in the region of the Arʹnon; and they did not come within the boundary of Moʹab, because Arʹnon was the boundary of Moʹab.

6848.label: Judges 11:19
6848.text: “‘After that Israel sent messengers to Siʹhon the king of the Amʹor·ites, the king of Heshʹbon, and Israel said to him: “Let us pass, please, through your land to my own place.”

6849.label: Judges 11:20
6849.text: And Siʹhon did not feel sure about Israel’s crossing through his territory, and Siʹhon went gathering all his people together and camping in Jaʹhaz and fighting against Israel.

6850.label: Judges 11:21
6850.text: At this Jehovah the God of Israel gave Siʹhon and all his people into Israel’s hand, so that they struck them and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amʹor·ites inhabiting that land.

6851.label: Judges 11:22
6851.text: Thus they took possession of all the territory of the Amʹor·ites from the Arʹnon as far as the Jabʹbok and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.

6852.label: Judges 11:23
6852.text: “‘And now Jehovah the God of Israel it was that dispossessed the Amʹor·ites from before his people Israel, and you, for your part, would dispossess them.

6853.label: Judges 11:24
6853.text: Is it not whomever Cheʹmosh your god causes you to dispossess that you will dispossess? And every one whom Jehovah our God has dispossessed from before us is the one we shall dispossess.

6854.label: Judges 11:25
6854.text: And now are you any better than Baʹlak the son of Zipʹpor, the king of Moʹab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

6855.label: Judges 11:26
6855.text: While Israel was dwelling in Heshʹbon and its dependent towns and in A·roʹer and its dependent towns and in all the cities that are by the banks of Arʹnon for three hundred years, why, then, did you never snatch them away during that time?

6856.label: Judges 11:27
6856.text: As for me, I have not sinned against you, but you are dealing wrong with me by fighting against me. Let Jehovah the Judge judge today between the sons of Israel and the sons of Amʹmon.’”

6857.label: Judges 11:28
6857.text: And the king of the sons of Amʹmon did not listen to the words of Jephʹthah that he had sent to him.

6858.label: Judges 11:29
6858.text: Jehovah’s spirit now came upon Jephʹthah, and he proceeded to pass through Gilʹe·ad and Ma·nasʹseh and to pass through Mizʹpeh of Gilʹe·ad, and from Mizʹpeh of Gilʹe·ad he passed along to the sons of Amʹmon.

6859.label: Judges 11:30
6859.text: Then Jephʹthah made a vow to Jehovah and said: “If you without fail give the sons of Amʹmon into my hand,

6860.label: Judges 11:31
6860.text: it must also occur that the one coming out, who comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Amʹmon, must also become Jehovah’s, and I must offer that one up as a burnt offering.”

6861.label: Judges 11:32
6861.text: So Jephʹthah passed along to the sons of Amʹmon to fight against them, and Jehovah proceeded to give them into his hand.

6862.label: Judges 11:33
6862.text: And he went striking them from A·roʹer all the way to Minʹnith —twenty cities—and as far as Aʹbel-kerʹa·mim with a very great slaughter. Thus the sons of Amʹmon were subdued before the sons of Israel.

6863.label: Judges 11:34
6863.text: Finally Jephʹthah came to Mizʹpah to his home, and, look! his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourine playing and dancing! Now she was absolutely the only child. Besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

6864.label: Judges 11:35
6864.text: And it came about that when he caught sight of her, he began to rip his garments and to say: “Alas, my daughter! You have indeed made me bend down, and you yourself have become the one I was ostracizing. And I—I have opened my mouth to Jehovah, and I am unable to turn back.”

6865.label: Judges 11:36
6865.text: But she said to him: “My father, if you have opened your mouth to Jehovah, do to me according to what has gone forth from your mouth, since Jehovah has executed acts of vengeance for you upon your enemies, the sons of Amʹmon.”

6866.label: Judges 11:37
6866.text: And she went on to say to her father: “Let this thing be done to me: Let me alone for two months, and let me go, and I will descend upon the mountains, and let me weep over my virginity, I and my girl companions.”

6867.label: Judges 11:38
6867.text: At this he said: “Go!” So he sent her away for two months; and she kept going, she with her girl companions, and weeping over her virginity upon the mountains.

6868.label: Judges 11:39
6868.text: And it came about at the end of two months that she made her return to her father, after which he carried out his vow that he had made toward her. As for her, she never had relations with a man. And it came to be a regulation in Israel:

6869.label: Judges 11:40
6869.text: From year to year the daughters of Israel would go to give commendation to the daughter of Jephʹthah the Gilʹe·ad·ite, four days in the year.

6870.label: Judges 12:1
6870.text: Then the men of Eʹphra·im were called together and crossed over northward and said to Jephʹthah: “Why is it that you crossed over to fight against the sons of Amʹmon, and to us you did not issue a call to go with you? Your very house we shall burn over you with fire.”

6871.label: Judges 12:2
6871.text: But Jephʹthah said to them: “I became a special contender, I and my people, with the sons of Amʹmon. And I proceeded to call to YOU for aid, and YOU did not save me out of their hand.

6872.label: Judges 12:3
6872.text: When I got to see that you were no savior, then I determined to put my soul in my own palm and go over against the sons of Amʹmon. At that Jehovah gave them into my hand. So why have YOU come up against me this day to fight against me?”

6873.label: Judges 12:4
6873.text: Immediately Jephʹthah collected all the men of Gilʹe·ad together and fought Eʹphra·im; and the men of Gilʹe·ad went striking Eʹphra·im down, for they had said: “Men escaped from Eʹphra·im is what YOU are, O Gilʹe·ad, inside of Eʹphra·im, inside of Ma·nasʹseh.”

6874.label: Judges 12:5
6874.text: And Gilʹe·ad got to capture the fords of the Jordan ahead of Eʹphra·im; and it occurred that when the escaping men of Eʹphra·im would say: “Let me pass over,” then the men of Gilʹe·ad would say to each one: “Are you an Eʹphra·im·ite?” When he would say: “No!”

6875.label: Judges 12:6
6875.text: then they would say to him: “Please say Shibʹbo·leth.” And he would say: “Sibʹbo·leth,” as he was unable to say the word correctly. And they would lay hold of him and slay him at the fords of the Jordan. So there fell at that time forty-two thousand out of Eʹphra·im.

6876.label: Judges 12:7
6876.text: And Jephʹthah continued to judge Israel for six years, after which Jephʹthah the Gilʹe·ad·ite died and was buried in his city in Gilʹe·ad.

6877.label: Judges 12:8
6877.text: And Ibʹzan from Bethʹle·hem began to judge Israel after him.

6878.label: Judges 12:9
6878.text: And he came to have thirty sons and thirty daughters. He sent outside and brought in thirty daughters for his sons from outside. And he continued to judge Israel for seven years.

6879.label: Judges 12:10
6879.text: Then Ibʹzan died and was buried in Bethʹle·hem.

6880.label: Judges 12:11
6880.text: And after him Eʹlon the Ze·buʹlu·nite began to judge Israel. And he continued to judge Israel ten years.

6881.label: Judges 12:12
6881.text: Then Eʹlon the Ze·buʹlu·nite died and was buried in Aiʹja·lon in the land of Zebʹu·lun.

6882.label: Judges 12:13
6882.text: And after him Abʹdon the son of Hilʹlel the Pirʹa·thon·ite began to judge Israel.

6883.label: Judges 12:14
6883.text: And he came to have forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy full-grown asses. And he continued to judge Israel eight years.

6884.label: Judges 12:15
6884.text: Then Abʹdon the son of Hilʹlel the Pirʹa·thon·ite died and was buried in Pirʹa·thon in the land of Eʹphra·im in the mountain of the A·malʹek·ite.

6885.label: Judges 13:1
6885.text: And the sons of Israel engaged again in doing what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, so that Jehovah gave them into the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines for forty years.

6886.label: Judges 13:2
6886.text: Meanwhile there happened to be a certain man of Zoʹrah of the family of the Danʹites, and his name was Ma·noʹah. And his wife was barren and had borne no child.

6887.label: Judges 13:3
6887.text: In time Jehovah’s angel appeared to the woman and said to her: “Look, now, you are barren and have borne no child. And you will certainly become pregnant and give birth to a son.

6888.label: Judges 13:4
6888.text: And now watch yourself, please, and do not drink wine or intoxicating liquor, and do not eat anything unclean.

6889.label: Judges 13:5
6889.text: For, look! you will be pregnant, and you will certainly give birth to a son, and no razor should come upon his head, because a Nazʹi·rite of God is what the child will become on leaving the belly; and he it is who will take the lead in saving Israel out of the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines.”

6890.label: Judges 13:6
6890.text: Then the woman went and said to her husband: “There was a man of the [true] God that came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the angel of the [true] God, very fear-inspiring. And I did not ask him from just where he was, neither did he tell me his name.
