6891.label: Judges 13:7
6891.text: But he said to me, ‘Look! You will be pregnant, and you will certainly give birth to a son. And now do not drink wine or intoxicating liquor, and do not eat any unclean thing, because a Nazʹi·rite of God is what the child will become on leaving the belly until the day of his death.’”

6892.label: Judges 13:8
6892.text: And Ma·noʹah began to entreat Jehovah and say: “Excuse me, Jehovah. The man of the [true] God that you just sent, let him, please, come again to us and instruct us as to what we ought to do to the child that will be born.”

6893.label: Judges 13:9
6893.text: Accordingly the [true] God listened to the voice of Ma·noʹah, and the angel of the [true] God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field, and Ma·noʹah her husband was not with her.

6894.label: Judges 13:10
6894.text: Immediately the woman hurried and ran and told her husband and said to him: “Look! The man that came the other day to me has appeared to me.”

6895.label: Judges 13:11
6895.text: At that Ma·noʹah got up and accompanied his wife and came to the man and said to him: “Are you the man that spoke to the woman?” to which he said: “I am.”

6896.label: Judges 13:12
6896.text: Then Ma·noʹah said: “Now let your words come true. What will become the child’s mode of life and his work?”

6897.label: Judges 13:13
6897.text: So Jehovah’s angel said to Ma·noʹah: “From everything that I mentioned to the woman she should keep herself.

6898.label: Judges 13:14
6898.text: Nothing at all that comes forth from the wine vine should she eat, and no wine or intoxicating liquor let her drink, and no unclean thing of any sort let her eat. Everything that I have commanded her let her keep.”

6899.label: Judges 13:15
6899.text: Ma·noʹah now said to Jehovah’s angel: “Let us, please, detain you and fix up a kid of the goats before you.”

6900.label: Judges 13:16
6900.text: But Jehovah’s angel said to Ma·noʹah: “If you detain me, I shall not feed myself on your bread; but if you will render up a burnt offering to Jehovah, you may offer it up.” For Ma·noʹah did not know that he was Jehovah’s angel.

6901.label: Judges 13:17
6901.text: Then Ma·noʹah said to Jehovah’s angel: “What is your name, that when your word comes true we shall certainly do you honor?”

6902.label: Judges 13:18
6902.text: However, Jehovah’s angel said to him: “Just why should you ask about my name, when it is a wonderful one?”

6903.label: Judges 13:19
6903.text: And Ma·noʹah proceeded to take the kid of the goats and the grain offering and to offer it upon the rock to Jehovah. And He was doing something in a wonderful way while Ma·noʹah and his wife were looking on.

6904.label: Judges 13:20
6904.text: So it came about that, as the flame ascended from off the altar heavenward, then Jehovah’s angel ascended in the flame of the altar while Ma·noʹah and his wife were looking on. At once they fell upon their faces to the earth.

6905.label: Judges 13:21
6905.text: And Jehovah’s angel did not repeat appearing to Ma·noʹah and his wife anymore. Then it was that Ma·noʹah knew that he had been Jehovah’s angel.

6906.label: Judges 13:22
6906.text: Consequently Ma·noʹah said to his wife: “We shall positively die, because it is God that we have seen.”

6907.label: Judges 13:23
6907.text: But his wife said to him: “If Jehovah had been delighted only to put us to death, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hand, and he would not have shown us all these things, and he would not as now have let us hear anything like this.”

6908.label: Judges 13:24
6908.text: Later the woman gave birth to a son and called his name Samson; and the boy kept getting bigger, and Jehovah continued to bless him.

6909.label: Judges 13:25
6909.text: In time Jehovah’s spirit started to impel him in Maʹha·neh-dan between Zoʹrah and Eshʹta·ol.

6910.label: Judges 14:1
6910.text: Then Samson went down to Timʹnah and saw a woman in Timʹnah of the daughters of the Phi·lisʹtines.

6911.label: Judges 14:2
6911.text: So he went up and told his father and his mother and said: “There is a woman that I have seen in Timʹnah of the daughters of the Phi·lisʹtines, and now get her for me as a wife.”

6912.label: Judges 14:3
6912.text: But his father and his mother said to him: “Is there not among the daughters of your brothers and among all my people a woman, so that you are going to take a wife from the uncircumcised Phi·lisʹtines?” Still Samson said to his father: “Get just her for me, because she is the one just right in my eyes.”

6913.label: Judges 14:4
6913.text: As for his father and his mother, they did not know that that was from Jehovah, that he was looking for an opportunity against the Phi·lisʹtines, as at that particular time the Phi·lisʹtines were ruling over Israel.

6914.label: Judges 14:5
6914.text: Accordingly Samson went on down with his father and his mother to Timʹnah. When he got as far as the vineyards of Timʹnah, why, look! a maned young lion roaring upon meeting him.

6915.label: Judges 14:6
6915.text: Then Jehovah’s spirit became operative upon him, so that he tore it in two, just as someone tears a male kid in two, and there was nothing at all in his hand. And he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.

6916.label: Judges 14:7
6916.text: And he continued on his way down and began to speak to the woman; and she was still right in Samson’s eyes.

6917.label: Judges 14:8
6917.text: Now after a while he went on back to take her home. Meantime he turned aside to look at the carcass of the lion, and there there was a swarm of bees in the lion’s corpse, and honey.

6918.label: Judges 14:9
6918.text: So he scraped it out into his palms and walked on, eating as he walked. When he rejoined his father and his mother, he at once gave them some, and they began to eat. And he did not tell them that it was out of the corpse of the lion that he had scraped the honey.

6919.label: Judges 14:10
6919.text: And his father continued on his way down to the woman, and Samson proceeded to hold a banquet there; for that was the way the young fellows used to do.

6920.label: Judges 14:11
6920.text: And it came about that, on their seeing him, they immediately took thirty groomsmen, that these should keep with him.

6921.label: Judges 14:12
6921.text: Then Samson said to them: “Let me, please, propound a riddle to YOU. If YOU will without fail tell it to me during the seven days of the banquet and YOU do solve it, I shall in that case have to give YOU thirty undergarments and thirty outfits of clothing.

6922.label: Judges 14:13
6922.text: But if YOU are unable to tell it to me, YOU yourselves also must give me thirty undergarments and thirty outfits of clothing.” At this they said to him: “Do propound your riddle, and let us hear it.”

6923.label: Judges 14:14
6923.text: So he said to them: “Out of the eater something to eat came forth,And out of the strong something sweet came forth.” And they proved unable to tell the riddle for three days.

6924.label: Judges 14:15
6924.text: And it came about on the fourth day that they began to say to Samson’s wife: “Fool your husband that he may tell us the riddle. Otherwise we shall burn you and the house of your father with fire. Was it to take our possessions that YOU people invited us here?”

6925.label: Judges 14:16
6925.text: Consequently Samson’s wife began to weep over him and to say: “You only hate me, you do, and you do not love me. There was a riddle that you propounded to the sons of my people, but to me you have not told it.” At this he said to her: “Why, to my own father and my own mother I have not told it, and ought I to tell it to you?”

6926.label: Judges 14:17
6926.text: But she kept weeping over him the seven days that the banquet continued for them, and it came about on the seventh day that finally he told her, because she had pressured him. Then she told the riddle to the sons of her people.

6927.label: Judges 14:18
6927.text: So the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before ever he could go into the interior room: “What is sweeter than honey,And what is stronger than a lion?” In turn he said to them:“If YOU had not plowed with my young cow, YOU would not have solved my riddle.”

6928.label: Judges 14:19
6928.text: And Jehovah’s spirit became operative upon him, so that he went down to Ashʹke·lon and struck down thirty men of theirs and took what he stripped off them and gave the outfits to the tellers of the riddle. And his anger continued hot, and he went his way up to his father’s house.

6929.label: Judges 14:20
6929.text: And Samson’s wife came to belong to a groomsman of his who had associated with him.

6930.label: Judges 15:1
6930.text: And it came about after a while, in the days of wheat harvest, that Samson went visiting his wife with a kid of the goats. So he said: “I will go in to my wife in the interior room.” And her father did not allow him to go in.

6931.label: Judges 15:2
6931.text: But her father said: “I really said to myself, ‘You must unquestionably hate her.’ Hence I gave her to your groomsman. Is not her younger sister better than she is? Let her, please, become yours instead of the other.”

6932.label: Judges 15:3
6932.text: However, Samson said to them: “This time I must be free of guilt against the Phi·lisʹtines in case I am dealing with them to their injury.”

6933.label: Judges 15:4
6933.text: And Samson went his way and proceeded to catch three hundred foxes and to take torches and turn tail to tail and put one torch between two tails, right in the middle.

6934.label: Judges 15:5
6934.text: With that he set fire to the torches and sent them out into the fields of standing grain of the Phi·lisʹtines. Thus he set on fire everything from sheaf to standing grain and the vineyards and the olive groves.

6935.label: Judges 15:6
6935.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines began to say: “Who did this?” Then they said: “It was Samson the son-in-law of the Timʹnite, because he took his wife and then gave her to his groomsman.” At that the Phi·lisʹtines went up and burned her and her father with fire.

6936.label: Judges 15:7
6936.text: In turn Samson said to them: “If YOU do like this, there is nothing but for me to avenge myself upon YOU, and afterward I shall quit.”

6937.label: Judges 15:8
6937.text: And he went smiting them, piling legs upon thighs with a great slaughter, after which he went down and began to dwell in a cleft of the crag Eʹtam.

6938.label: Judges 15:9
6938.text: Later the Phi·lisʹtines came up and camped in Judah and went tramping about in Leʹhi.

6939.label: Judges 15:10
6939.text: Then the men of Judah said: “Why have YOU come up against us?” to which they said: “It is to tie Samson that we have come up, to do to him just as he has done to us.”

6940.label: Judges 15:11
6940.text: So three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the crag Eʹtam and said to Samson: “Do you not know that the Phi·lisʹtines are ruling over us? So what does this mean that you have done to us?” Then he said to them: “Just as they did to me is the way I have done to them.”

6941.label: Judges 15:12
6941.text: But they said to him: “It is to tie you that we have come down, to give you into the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines.” At that Samson said to them: “Swear to me that YOU yourselves will not assault me.”

6942.label: Judges 15:13
6942.text: And they went on to say to him: “No, but we shall merely tie you, and we will give you into their hand; but we shall by no means put you to death.” Accordingly they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up out of the crag.

6943.label: Judges 15:14
6943.text: He, for his part, came as far as Leʹhi, and the Phi·lisʹtines, for their part, shouted exultantly at meeting him. And Jehovah’s spirit became operative upon him, and the ropes that were upon his arms came to be like linen threads that have been scorched with fire, so that his fetters melted off his hands.

6944.label: Judges 15:15
6944.text: He now found a moist jawbone of a male ass and thrust his hand out and took it and went striking down a thousand men with it.

6945.label: Judges 15:16
6945.text: Then Samson said: “With the jawbone of a male ass—one heap, two heaps! With the jawbone of a male ass I have struck down a thousand men.”

6946.label: Judges 15:17
6946.text: And it came about that when he finished speaking, he immediately threw the jawbone out of his hand and called that place Raʹmath-leʹhi.

6947.label: Judges 15:18
6947.text: Now he became very thirsty, and he began to call on Jehovah and say: “It was you that gave this great salvation into the hand of your servant, and now shall I die of thirst and must I fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?”

6948.label: Judges 15:19
6948.text: So God split open a mortar-shaped hollow that was in Leʹhi, and water began to come out of it, and he proceeded to drink, after which his spirit returned and he revived. That is why he called its name En-hak·korʹe, which is in Leʹhi down to this day.

6949.label: Judges 15:20
6949.text: And he continued to judge Israel in the days of the Phi·lisʹtines twenty years.

6950.label: Judges 16:1
6950.text: Once Samson went to Gaʹza and saw a prostitute woman there and came in to her.

6951.label: Judges 16:2
6951.text: And report was made to the Gaʹzites, saying: “Samson has come in here.” So they surrounded him and lay in wait for him all night long in the city gate. And they kept quiet the whole night, saying: “As soon as the morning gets light, we must also kill him.”

6952.label: Judges 16:3
6952.text: However, Samson kept lying till midnight and then rose at midnight and grabbed hold of the doors of the city gate and the two side posts and pulled them out along with the bar and put them upon his shoulders and went carrying them up to the top of the mountain that is in front of Heʹbron.

6953.label: Judges 16:4
6953.text: And it came about after that that he fell in love with a woman in the torrent valley of Soʹrek, and her name was De·liʹlah.

6954.label: Judges 16:5
6954.text: And the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines proceeded to come up to her and to say to her: “Fool him and see in what his great power is and with what we can prevail over him and with what we are certain to tie him so as to master him; and we, for our part, shall give you each one thousand one hundred silver pieces.”

6955.label: Judges 16:6
6955.text: Later De·liʹlah said to Samson: “Do tell me, please, In what is your great power and with what can you be tied for one to master you?”

6956.label: Judges 16:7
6956.text: Then Samson said to her: “If they tie me with seven still-moist sinews that have not been dried out, I must also grow weak and become like an ordinary man.”

6957.label: Judges 16:8
6957.text: So the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines brought up to her seven still-moist sinews that had not been dried out. Later she tied him with them.

6958.label: Judges 16:9
6958.text: Now the ambush was sitting in the interior room of hers, and she began to say to him: “The Phi·lisʹtines are upon you, Samson!” At that he tore the sinews in two, just as a twisted thread of tow is torn in two when it smells fire. And his power did not become known.

6959.label: Judges 16:10
6959.text: Subsequently De·liʹlah said to Samson: “Look! You have trifled with me that you might speak lies to me. Now tell me, do please, with what you can be tied.”

6960.label: Judges 16:11
6960.text: So he said to her: “If they tie me tight with new ropes with which no work has been done, I must also grow weak and become like an ordinary man.”

6961.label: Judges 16:12
6961.text: So De·liʹlah took new ropes and tied him with them and said to him: “The Phi·lisʹtines are upon you, Samson!” All the while the ambush was sitting in the interior room. At that he tore them in two from off his arms like a thread.

6962.label: Judges 16:13
6962.text: After that De·liʹlah said to Samson: “Up till now you have trifled with me that you might speak lies to me. Do tell me with what you can be tied.” Then he said to her: “If you will weave the seven braids of my head with the warp thread.”

6963.label: Judges 16:14
6963.text: Accordingly she fixed them with the pin, after which she said to him: “The Phi·lisʹtines are upon you, Samson!” So he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the loom pin and the warp thread.

6964.label: Judges 16:15
6964.text: She now said to him: “How dare you say, ‘I do love you,’ when your heart is not with me? These three times you have trifled with me and have not told me in what your great power is.”

6965.label: Judges 16:16
6965.text: And it came about that because she pressured him with her words all the time and kept urging him, his soul got to be impatient to the point of dying.

6966.label: Judges 16:17
6966.text: Finally he disclosed to her all his heart and said to her: “A razor has never come upon my head, because I am a Nazʹi·rite of God from my mother’s belly. If I did get shaved, my power also would certainly depart from me, and I should indeed grow weak and become like all other men.”

6967.label: Judges 16:18
6967.text: When De·liʹlah got to see that he had disclosed to her all his heart, she immediately sent and called the Phi·lisʹtine axis lords, saying: “Come up this time, for he has disclosed to me all his heart.” And the Phi·lisʹtine axis lords came up to her that they might bring up the money in their hand.

6968.label: Judges 16:19
6968.text: And she proceeded to make him sleep upon her knees. Then she called the man and had him shave off the seven braids of his head, after which she started to show the mastery of him, and his power kept departing from upon him.

6969.label: Judges 16:20
6969.text: Now she said: “The Phi·lisʹtines are upon you, Samson!” At that he woke up from his sleep and said: “I shall go out as at other times and shake myself free.” And he himself did not know that it was Jehovah that had departed from him.

6970.label: Judges 16:21
6970.text: So the Phi·lisʹtines grabbed hold of him and bored his eyes out and brought him down to Gaʹza and bound him with two fetters of copper; and he came to be a grinder in the prison house.

6971.label: Judges 16:22
6971.text: Meanwhile the hair of his head started to grow luxuriantly as soon as he had been shaved.

6972.label: Judges 16:23
6972.text: As for the Phi·lisʹtine axis lords, they gathered together to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Daʹgon their god and for rejoicing, and they kept saying: “Our god has given into our hand Samson our enemy!”

6973.label: Judges 16:24
6973.text: When the people got to see him, they at once gave way to praising their god, “because,” said they, “our god has given into our hand our enemy and the devastator of our land and the one who multiplied our slain.”

6974.label: Judges 16:25
6974.text: And it came about that because their heart was merry, they began to say: “Call Samson that he may offer us some amusement.” So they called Samson out of the prison house that he might make sport before them; and they proceeded to stand him between the pillars.

6975.label: Judges 16:26
6975.text: Then Samson said to the boy that was holding him by his hand: “Do permit me to feel the pillars upon which the house is firmly established and let me lean against them.”

6976.label: Judges 16:27
6976.text: (Incidentally, the house was full of men and women and all the Phi·lisʹtine axis lords were there; and upon the roof there were about three thousand men and women who were looking on while Samson offered some amusement.)

6977.label: Judges 16:28
6977.text: Samson now called to Jehovah and said: “Sovereign Lord Jehovah, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, just this once, O you the [true] God, and let me avenge myself upon the Phi·lisʹtines with vengeance for one of my two eyes.”

6978.label: Judges 16:29
6978.text: With that Samson braced himself against the two middle pillars upon which the house was firmly established, and got a grasp on them, one with his right and the other with his left hand.

6979.label: Judges 16:30
6979.text: And Samson proceeded to say: “Let my soul die with the Phi·lisʹtines.” Then he bent himself with power, and the house went falling upon the axis lords and upon all the people that were in it, so that the dead that he put to death in his own death came to be more than those he had put to death during his lifetime.

6980.label: Judges 16:31
6980.text: Later his brothers and all the household of his father came on down and lifted him up and brought him up and buried him between Zoʹrah and Eshʹta·ol in the burial place of Ma·noʹah his father. As for him, he had judged Israel twenty years.

6981.label: Judges 17:1
6981.text: Now there happened to be a man of the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im whose name was Miʹcah.

6982.label: Judges 17:2
6982.text: In time he said to his mother: “The thousand one hundred silver pieces that were taken from you and over which you pronounced a curse and also said it in my hearing—look! the silver is with me. It was I who took it.” At that his mother said: “Blessed may my son be of Jehovah.”

6983.label: Judges 17:3
6983.text: Accordingly he gave back the thousand one hundred pieces of silver to his mother; and his mother went on to say: “I must without fail sanctify the silver to Jehovah from my hand for my son, so as to make a carved image and a molten statue; and now I shall give it back to you.”

6984.label: Judges 17:4
6984.text: So he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took two hundred silver pieces and gave them to the silversmith. And he went making a carved image and a molten statue; and it got to be in Miʹcah’s house.

6985.label: Judges 17:5
6985.text: As for the man Miʹcah, he had a house of gods, and he proceeded to make an ephʹod and teraphim and to fill the hand of one of his sons with power, that he might serve as priest for him.

6986.label: Judges 17:6
6986.text: In those days there was no king in Israel. As for everybody, what was right in his own eyes he was accustomed to do.

6987.label: Judges 17:7
6987.text: Now there happened to be a young man of Bethʹle·hem in Judah of the family of Judah, and he was a Levite. And he was residing there for a time.

6988.label: Judges 17:8
6988.text: And the man proceeded to go from the city of Bethʹle·hem in Judah to reside for a time wherever he might find a place. At length while going his way he came into the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im as far as the house of Miʹcah.

6989.label: Judges 17:9
6989.text: Then Miʹcah said to him: “Where do you come from?” At that he said to him: “I am a Levite from Bethʹle·hem in Judah, and I am on my way to reside for a time wherever I may find a place.”

6990.label: Judges 17:10
6990.text: So Miʹcah said to him: “Do dwell with me and serve as a father and priest for me, and I, for my part, shall give you ten silver pieces a year and the usual outfit of garments and your sustenance.” Accordingly the Levite went in.

6991.label: Judges 17:11
6991.text: Thus the Levite took it upon himself to dwell with the man, and the young man got to be as one of his sons to him.

6992.label: Judges 17:12
6992.text: Furthermore, Miʹcah filled the hand of the Levite with power, that the young man might serve as a priest for him and might continue in the house of Miʹcah.

6993.label: Judges 17:13
6993.text: Hence Miʹcah said: “Now I do know that Jehovah will do me good, because the Levite has become priest for me.”

6994.label: Judges 18:1
6994.text: In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danʹites was looking for an inheritance for itself to dwell there; because up to that day an inheritance had not fallen to them in the midst of the tribes of Israel.

6995.label: Judges 18:2
6995.text: Eventually the sons of Dan sent five men of their family, men from among them, men who were valiant fellows, out from Zoʹrah and Eshʹta·ol, to spy out the land and to explore it. So they said to them: “Go, explore the land.” In time they came into the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im as far as the house of Miʹcah and got to spend the night there.

6996.label: Judges 18:3
6996.text: While they were close by the house of Miʹcah, they recognized the voice of the young man, the Levite, so that they turned aside there. And they proceeded to say to him: “Who brought you here, and what are you doing in this place, and what interest do you have here?”

6997.label: Judges 18:4
6997.text: In turn he said to them: “Thus and so Miʹcah did for me that he might hire me, and that I might serve as priest for him.”

6998.label: Judges 18:5
6998.text: Then they said to him: “Inquire, please, of God that we may know whether our way on which we are going will be successful.”

6999.label: Judges 18:6
6999.text: So the priest said to them: “Go in peace. It is before Jehovah that YOUR way is in which YOU go.”

7000.label: Judges 18:7
7000.text: Accordingly the five men went on and came to Laʹish and saw how the people that were within it were dwelling in self-reliance according to the custom of the Si·doʹni·ans, quiet and unsuspecting, and there was no oppressive conqueror that was molesting a thing in the land, while they were far off from the Si·doʹni·ans and they had nothing to do with mankind.

7001.label: Judges 18:8
7001.text: At length they came to their brothers at Zoʹrah and Eshʹta·ol, and their brothers began to say to them: “How was it with YOU?”

7002.label: Judges 18:9
7002.text: At this they said: “Do get up, and let us go up against them; for we have seen the land, and, look! it is very good. And YOU are hesitant. Do not be sluggish about walking to come in to take possession of the land.

7003.label: Judges 18:10
7003.text: When YOU come in, YOU will come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is quite wide; for God has given it into YOUR hand, a place where there is no lack of any sort of thing that is in the earth.”

7004.label: Judges 18:11
7004.text: Then six hundred men girded with weapons of war, out of the family of the Danʹites, departed from there, that is, from Zoʹrah and Eshʹta·ol.

7005.label: Judges 18:12
7005.text: And they got on their way up and went camping at Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim in Judah. That is why they have called that place Maʹha·neh-dan down to this day. Look! It is west of Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim.

7006.label: Judges 18:13
7006.text: After that they passed along from there to the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im and came as far as the house of Miʹcah.

7007.label: Judges 18:14
7007.text: Then the five men that had gone to spy out the land of Laʹish answered and said to their brothers: “Did YOU know that there are in these houses an ephʹod and teraphim and a carved image and a molten statue? And now have in mind what YOU ought to do.”

7008.label: Judges 18:15
7008.text: So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite, at the house of Miʹcah, and began to ask how he was getting along.

7009.label: Judges 18:16
7009.text: All the while the six hundred men girded with their weapons of war, who were of the sons of Dan, were standing at the entrance of the gate.

7010.label: Judges 18:17
7010.text: The five men that had gone to spy out the land now went on up, that they might enter in there to take the carved image and the ephʹod and the teraphim and the molten image. (And the priest was standing at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men girded with weapons of war.)

7011.label: Judges 18:18
7011.text: And these went into the house of Miʹcah and proceeded to take the carved image, the ephʹod and the teraphim and the molten image. At that the priest said to them: “What are YOU doing?”

7012.label: Judges 18:19
7012.text: But they said to him: “Be quiet. Put your hand over your mouth, and go with us and become a father and a priest for us. Which is better, for you to continue a priest to the house of one man or for you to become a priest to a tribe and family in Israel?”

7013.label: Judges 18:20
7013.text: At this the heart of the priest was pleased, and he now took the ephʹod and the teraphim and the carved image and came into the midst of the people.

7014.label: Judges 18:21
7014.text: Then they turned and went their way and put the little ones and the livestock and the valuable things ahead of them.

7015.label: Judges 18:22
7015.text: They themselves had got a distance away from the house of Miʹcah when the men who were in the houses that were close by the house of Miʹcah were called together and tried to catch up with the sons of Dan.

7016.label: Judges 18:23
7016.text: When they kept crying out to the sons of Dan, then they turned their faces and said to Miʹcah: “What is the matter with you that you have been called together?”

7017.label: Judges 18:24
7017.text: So he said: “My gods that I made YOU have taken, the priest too, and YOU go YOUR way, and what do I have anymore? How, then, is it that YOU can say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’”

7018.label: Judges 18:25
7018.text: At this the sons of Dan said to him: “Do not let your voice be heard close to us, for fear that men bitter of soul may assault YOU people, and you have to forfeit your own soul and the soul of your household.”

7019.label: Judges 18:26
7019.text: And the sons of Dan kept going on their way; and Miʹcah got to see that they were stronger than he was, and so he turned and went back to his house.

7020.label: Judges 18:27
7020.text: As for them, they took what Miʹcah had made and the priest that had become his, and they kept going toward Laʹish, against a people quiet and unsuspecting. And they proceeded to strike them with the edge of the sword, and the city they burned with fire.

7021.label: Judges 18:28
7021.text: And there was no deliverer, for it was far away from Siʹdon, and they had nothing at all to do with mankind; and it was in the low plain that belonged to Beth-reʹhob. Then they built the city and took up dwelling in it.

7022.label: Judges 18:29
7022.text: Furthermore, they called the name of the city Dan by the name of their father, Dan, who had been born to Israel. Nevertheless, Laʹish was the city’s name at first.

7023.label: Judges 18:30
7023.text: After that the sons of Dan stood up the carved image for themselves; and Jonʹa·than the son of Gerʹshom, Moses’ son, he and his sons became priests to the tribe of the Danʹites until the day of the land’s being taken into exile.

7024.label: Judges 18:31
7024.text: And they kept the carved image of Miʹcah, which he had made, set up for themselves all the days that the house of the [true] God continued in Shiʹloh.

7025.label: Judges 19:1
7025.text: Now it happened in those days that there was no king in Israel. And it came about that a certain Levite was residing for a time in the remotest parts of the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im. In time he took as his wife a concubine from Bethʹle·hem in Judah.

7026.label: Judges 19:2
7026.text: And his concubine began to commit fornication against him. Finally she went away from him to the house of her father at Bethʹle·hem in Judah and continued there fully four months.

7027.label: Judges 19:3
7027.text: Then her husband got up and went after her to speak consolingly to her so as to bring her back; and there were with him his attendant and a couple of he-asses. So she had him come into her father’s house. When the father of the young woman got to see him, he at once rejoiced to meet him.

7028.label: Judges 19:4
7028.text: Consequently his father-in-law, the young woman’s father, took hold of him, so that he continued to dwell with him three days; and they would eat and drink, and he would stay overnight there.

7029.label: Judges 19:5
7029.text: And it came about on the fourth day, when they got up early in the morning as usual, he now rose to go, but the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law: “Sustain your heart with a bit of bread and afterward YOU people may go.”

7030.label: Judges 19:6
7030.text: So they sat down, and both of them began to eat and to drink together; after which the father of the young woman said to the man: “Come on, please, and stay overnight, and let your heart feel good.”

7031.label: Judges 19:7
7031.text: When the man rose to go, his father-in-law kept begging him, so that he stayed overnight there again.

7032.label: Judges 19:8
7032.text: When he got up early in the morning on the fifth day to go, the father of the young woman then said: “Please, take sustenance for your heart.” And they lingered until the fading away of the day. And both of them kept eating.

7033.label: Judges 19:9
7033.text: The man now rose to go, he and his concubine and his attendant; but his father-in-law, the young woman’s father, said to him: “Look, now! The day has declined toward becoming evening. Please, STAY overnight. Here the day is settling down. Stay here overnight, and let your heart feel good. And tomorrow YOU people must get up early for YOUR journey, and you must go to your tent.”

7034.label: Judges 19:10
7034.text: However, the man did not consent to stay overnight, but he rose and got on his way and came as far as in front of Jeʹbus, that is to say, Jerusalem; and with him there were the couple of he-asses saddled up, and his concubine and his attendant.

7035.label: Judges 19:11
7035.text: While they were close by Jeʹbus, as the daylight had gone down considerably, the attendant now said to his master: “O come, now, and let us turn aside to this city of the Jebʹu·sites and stay in it overnight.”

7036.label: Judges 19:12
7036.text: But his master said to him: “Let us not turn aside to a city of foreigners who are no part of the sons of Israel; and we have to pass on as far as Gibʹe·ah.”

7037.label: Judges 19:13
7037.text: And he went on to say to his attendant: “Come and let us approach one of the places, and we must stay overnight either in Gibʹe·ah or in Raʹmah.”

7038.label: Judges 19:14
7038.text: So they passed along and kept on their way, and the sun began to set upon them when near to Gibʹe·ah, which belongs to Benjamin.

7039.label: Judges 19:15
7039.text: Consequently they turned aside there to go in to stay overnight in Gibʹe·ah. And they proceeded to go in and sit down in the public square of the city, and there was nobody taking them on into the house to stay overnight.

7040.label: Judges 19:16
7040.text: Eventually, look! an old man coming in from his work in the field at evening, and the man was from the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im, and he was residing for a time in Gibʹe·ah; but the men of the place were Benʹja·mites.

7041.label: Judges 19:17
7041.text: When he raised his eyes he got to see the man, the traveler, in the public square of the city. So the old man said: “Where are you going, and where do you come from?”

7042.label: Judges 19:18
7042.text: In turn he said to him: “We are passing along from Bethʹle·hem in Judah to the remotest parts of the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im. That is where I am from, but I went to Bethʹle·hem in Judah; and it is to my own house that I am going, and there is nobody taking me on into the house.

7043.label: Judges 19:19
7043.text: And there are both straw and fodder for our he-asses, and there are both bread and wine for me and your slave girl and for the attendant with your servant. There is no lack of a single thing.”

7044.label: Judges 19:20
7044.text: However, the old man said: “May you have peace! Just let any lack of yours be upon me. Only do not stay overnight in the public square.”

7045.label: Judges 19:21
7045.text: With that he brought him into his house and threw mash to the he-asses. Then they washed their feet and began to eat and drink.

7046.label: Judges 19:22
7046.text: While they were making their hearts feel good, look! the men of the city, mere good-for-nothing men, surrounded the house, shoving one another against the door; and they kept saying to the old man, the owner of the house: “Bring out the man that came into your house, that we may have intercourse with him.”

7047.label: Judges 19:23
7047.text: At that the owner of the house went on out to them and said to them: “No, my brothers, do not do anything wrong, please, since this man has come into my house. Do not commit this disgraceful folly.

7048.label: Judges 19:24
7048.text: Here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. Let me bring them out, please, and YOU rape them and do to them what is good in YOUR eyes. But to this man YOU must not do this disgraceful, foolish thing.”

7049.label: Judges 19:25
7049.text: And the men did not want to listen to him. Hence the man took hold of his concubine and brought her forth to them outside; and they began to have intercourse with her, and kept on abusing her all night long until the morning, after which they sent her off at the ascending of the dawn.

7050.label: Judges 19:26
7050.text: Then the woman came as it was turning to morning, and fell down at the entrance of the man’s house where her master was, —until daylight.

7051.label: Judges 19:27
7051.text: Later her master rose up in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to get on his way, and, look! the woman, his concubine, fallen at the entrance of the house with her hands upon the threshold!

7052.label: Judges 19:28
7052.text: So he said to her: “Rise up, and let us go.” But there was no one answering. At that the man took her upon the ass and rose up and went to his place.

7053.label: Judges 19:29
7053.text: Then he entered his house and took the slaughtering knife and laid hold of his concubine and cut her up according to her bones into twelve pieces and sent her into every territory of Israel.

7054.label: Judges 19:30
7054.text: And it occurred that everybody seeing it said: “Such a thing as this has never been brought about or been seen from the day that the sons of Israel went up out of the land of Egypt down to this day. Set YOUR hearts upon it, take counsel and speak.”

7055.label: Judges 20:1
7055.text: Consequently all the sons of Israel went out and the assembly congregated themselves as one man, from Dan down to Beʹer-sheʹba along with the land of Gilʹe·ad, to Jehovah at Mizʹpah.

7056.label: Judges 20:2
7056.text: So the keymen of all the people and all the tribes of Israel took their station in the congregation of the people of the [true] God, four hundred thousand men on foot who drew the sword.

7057.label: Judges 20:3
7057.text: And the sons of Benjamin got to hear that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizʹpah. Then the sons of Israel said: “SPEAK. How has this bad thing been brought about?”

7058.label: Judges 20:4
7058.text: At this the man, the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said: “It was to Gibʹe·ah, which belongs to Benjamin, that I came, I and my concubine, to stay overnight.

7059.label: Judges 20:5
7059.text: And the landowners of Gibʹe·ah proceeded to rise up against me and to surround the house against me by night. It was I that they figured on killing, but it was my concubine that they raped, and she gradually died.

7060.label: Judges 20:6
7060.text: Hence I grasped my concubine and cut her up and sent her into every field of Israel’s inheritance, because they had carried on loose conduct and disgraceful folly in Israel.

7061.label: Judges 20:7
7061.text: Look! All YOU sons of Israel, give YOUR word and counsel here.”

7062.label: Judges 20:8
7062.text: So all the people rose up as one man, saying: “We shall not go any of us to his tent, nor shall we turn aside any of us to his house.

7063.label: Judges 20:9
7063.text: And now this is the thing that we shall do to Gibʹe·ah. Let us go up by lot against it.

7064.label: Judges 20:10
7064.text: And we must take ten men out of a hundred of all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to procure provisions for the people, that they may take action by going against Gibʹe·ah of Benjamin, in view of all the disgraceful folly that they did in Israel.”

7065.label: Judges 20:11
7065.text: Thus all the men of Israel were gathered against the city as one man, as allies.

7066.label: Judges 20:12
7066.text: Accordingly the tribes of Israel sent men to all the tribesmen of Benjamin, saying: “What is this bad thing that has been brought about among YOU?

7067.label: Judges 20:13
7067.text: And now give over the men, the good-for-nothing men, that are in Gibʹe·ah, that we may put them to death, and let us clear out what is bad from Israel.” And the sons of Benjamin did not want to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.

7068.label: Judges 20:14
7068.text: Then the sons of Benjamin went gathering together out of the cities to Gibʹe·ah to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.

7069.label: Judges 20:15
7069.text: So the sons of Benjamin got to be mustered on that day from the cities, twenty-six thousand men drawing sword, apart from the inhabitants of Gibʹe·ah, of whom seven hundred chosen men were mustered.

7070.label: Judges 20:16
7070.text: Out of all this people there were seven hundred chosen men left-handed. Every one of these was a slinger of stones to a hairbreadth and would not miss.

7071.label: Judges 20:17
7071.text: And the men of Israel were mustered apart from Benjamin, four hundred thousand men drawing sword. Every one of these was a man of war.

7072.label: Judges 20:18
7072.text: And they proceeded to rise up and go on up to Bethʹel and to inquire of God. Then the sons of Israel said: “Who of us should go up in the lead to the battle against the sons of Benjamin?” To this Jehovah said: “Judah in the lead.”

7073.label: Judges 20:19
7073.text: After that the sons of Israel rose up in the morning and camped against Gibʹe·ah.

7074.label: Judges 20:20
7074.text: The men of Israel now went out to battle against Benjamin; and the men of Israel proceeded to draw up in battle formation against them at Gibʹe·ah.

7075.label: Judges 20:21
7075.text: So the sons of Benjamin came on out from Gibʹe·ah and brought twenty-two thousand men in Israel down to ruin to the earth on that day.

7076.label: Judges 20:22
7076.text: However, the people, the men of Israel, showed themselves courageous and again went drawing up in battle formation in the place where they had drawn up in formation on the first day.

7077.label: Judges 20:23
7077.text: Then the sons of Israel went up and wept before Jehovah until the evening and inquired of Jehovah, saying: “Shall I again approach for battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother?” To this Jehovah said: “Go up against him.”

7078.label: Judges 20:24
7078.text: Accordingly the sons of Israel drew near to the sons of Benjamin on the second day.

7079.label: Judges 20:25
7079.text: In turn Benjamin came on out from Gibʹe·ah to meet them on the second day and brought a further eighteen thousand men among the sons of Israel down to ruin to the earth, all of these drawing sword.

7080.label: Judges 20:26
7080.text: At that all the sons of Israel, even all the people, went on up and came to Bethʹel and wept and sat there before Jehovah and fasted on that day until the evening and offered up burnt offerings and communion offerings before Jehovah.

7081.label: Judges 20:27
7081.text: After that the sons of Israel inquired of Jehovah, as it was there that the ark of the covenant of the [true] God was in those days.

7082.label: Judges 20:28
7082.text: Now Phinʹe·has the son of El·e·aʹzar, the son of Aaron, was standing before it in those days, saying: “Shall I go out yet again to battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother or shall I cease to?” To this Jehovah said: “Go up, because tomorrow I shall give him into your hand.”

7083.label: Judges 20:29
7083.text: Then Israel set men in ambush against Gibʹe·ah all around.

7084.label: Judges 20:30
7084.text: And the sons of Israel proceeded to go up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day, and to draw up in formation against Gibʹe·ah the same as at the other times.

7085.label: Judges 20:31
7085.text: When the sons of Benjamin went on out to meet the people, they were drawn away from the city. Then, the same as at the other times, they started to strike down some of the people mortally wounded on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethʹel and the other to Gibʹe·ah, in the field, about thirty men in Israel.

7086.label: Judges 20:32
7086.text: So the sons of Benjamin began to say: “They are suffering defeat before us the same as at the first.” As for the sons of Israel, they said: “Let us flee, and we shall certainly draw them away from the city onto the highways.”

7087.label: Judges 20:33
7087.text: And all the men of Israel rose up from their places and went drawing up in formation at Baʹal-taʹmar, while those of Israel in ambush were making a charge out of their places in the vicinity of Gibʹe·ah.

7088.label: Judges 20:34
7088.text: Thus ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel came in front of Gibʹe·ah, and the fighting was heavy; and the Benʹja·mites did not know that calamity was impending over them.

7089.label: Judges 20:35
7089.text: And Jehovah proceeded to defeat Benjamin before Israel, so that the sons of Israel on that day brought down to ruin in Benjamin twenty-five thousand one hundred men, all of these drawing sword.

7090.label: Judges 20:36
7090.text: However, the sons of Benjamin imagined that the men of Israel faced defeat when they kept giving ground to Benjamin because they trusted in the ambush that they had set against Gibʹe·ah.

7091.label: Judges 20:37
7091.text: As for the ambush, they acted quickly and went dashing toward Gibʹe·ah. Then the ambush spread out and struck all the city with the edge of the sword.

7092.label: Judges 20:38
7092.text: Now the men of Israel had come to the arrangement with the ambush for them to make a smoke signal go up from the city.

7093.label: Judges 20:39
7093.text: When the sons of Israel turned around in the battle, Benjamin started to strike down about thirty men mortally wounded among the men of Israel, for they said: “They are unquestionably suffering nothing but defeat before us just as in the first battle.”

7094.label: Judges 20:40
7094.text: And the signal started to go up from the city as a pillar of smoke. So when Benjamin turned his face back, look! the whole city went up heavenward.

7095.label: Judges 20:41
7095.text: And the men of Israel made an about-face, and the men of Benjamin were disturbed, for they saw that calamity had reached them.

7096.label: Judges 20:42
7096.text: Hence they turned before the men of Israel in the direction of the wilderness, and the battle followed them up closely, while the men from out of the cities were bringing them down to ruin in their midst.

7097.label: Judges 20:43
7097.text: They surrounded Benjamin. They pursued him without a place to rest. They trampled him down directly in front of Gibʹe·ah toward the rising of the sun.

7098.label: Judges 20:44
7098.text: Finally there fell eighteen thousand men of Benjamin, all of these being valiant men.

7099.label: Judges 20:45
7099.text: Thus they turned and went fleeing to the wilderness to the crag of Rimʹmon. And they made a gleaning of five thousand men of them on the highways, and they kept following closely after them as far as Giʹdom and so struck down two thousand more men of them.

7100.label: Judges 20:46
7100.text: And all those of Benjamin that fell on that day amounted at last to twenty-five thousand men drawing sword, all these being valiant men.

7101.label: Judges 20:47
7101.text: But six hundred men turned and went fleeing to the wilderness to the crag of Rimʹmon, and they continued to dwell on the crag of Rimʹmon four months.

7102.label: Judges 20:48
7102.text: And the men of Israel came back against the sons of Benjamin and went striking with the edge of the sword those of the city, [from] men to domestic animal up to all that were found. Also, all the cities that were found they consigned to the fire.

7103.label: Judges 21:1
7103.text: Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizʹpah, saying: “Not a man of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife.”

7104.label: Judges 21:2
7104.text: Consequently the people came to Bethʹel and kept sitting there before the [true] God until the evening and continued to raise their voice and indulge in a great deal of weeping.

7105.label: Judges 21:3
7105.text: And they would say: “Why, O Jehovah the God of Israel, has this occurred in Israel, for one tribe to be missing today from Israel?”

7106.label: Judges 21:4
7106.text: And it came about the next day that the people proceeded to get up early and to build an altar there and to offer up burnt offerings and communion offerings.

7107.label: Judges 21:5
7107.text: Then the sons of Israel said: “Who is there out of all the tribes of Israel that has not come up in the congregation to Jehovah, for there is a great oath that has taken place respecting the one that has not come up to Jehovah at Mizʹpah, saying, ‘Let him be put to death without fail.’”

7108.label: Judges 21:6
7108.text: And the sons of Israel began to feel regret over Benjamin their brother. So they said: “Today one tribe has been chopped off from Israel.

7109.label: Judges 21:7
7109.text: What shall we do to those who are left over as to wives, now that we ourselves have sworn by Jehovah not to give them any of our daughters as wives?”

7110.label: Judges 21:8
7110.text: And they went on to say: “Which one out of the tribes of Israel is it that has not come up to Jehovah at Mizʹpah?” And, look! no one had come into the camp from Jaʹbesh-gilʹe·ad to the congregation.

7111.label: Judges 21:9
7111.text: When the people were counted, well, look! there was not a man there from the inhabitants of Jaʹbesh-gilʹe·ad.

7112.label: Judges 21:10
7112.text: Hence the assembly proceeded to send twelve thousand of the most valiant men there and to command them, saying: “Go, and YOU must strike the inhabitants of Jaʹbesh-gilʹe·ad with the edge of the sword, even the women and the little ones.

7113.label: Judges 21:11
7113.text: And this is the thing that YOU should do: Every male and every woman that has experienced lying with a male YOU should devote to destruction.”

7114.label: Judges 21:12
7114.text: However, they found out of the inhabitants of Jaʹbesh-gilʹe·ad four hundred girls, virgins, that had not had intercourse with a man by lying with a male. So they brought them to the camp at Shiʹloh, which is in the land of Caʹnaan.

7115.label: Judges 21:13
7115.text: And all the assembly now sent and spoke to the sons of Benjamin that were on the crag of Rimʹmon and offered them peace.

7116.label: Judges 21:14
7116.text: Accordingly Benjamin came back at that time. Then they gave them the women that they had preserved alive from the women of Jaʹbesh-gilʹe·ad; but they did not find enough for them.

7117.label: Judges 21:15
7117.text: And the people felt regret over Benjamin because Jehovah had made a rupture between the tribes of Israel.

7118.label: Judges 21:16
7118.text: Consequently the older men of the assembly said: “What shall we do to the men that are left over as to wives, for womankind has been annihilated out of Benjamin?”

7119.label: Judges 21:17
7119.text: Then they said: “There should be a possession for those who have escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe might not be wiped out of Israel.

7120.label: Judges 21:18
7120.text: As for us, we are not allowed to give them wives from our daughters, because the sons of Israel have sworn, saying, ‘Cursed is the one that gives a wife to Benjamin.’”

7121.label: Judges 21:19
7121.text: Finally they said: “Look! There is a festival of Jehovah from year to year in Shiʹloh, which is to the north of Bethʹel, toward the east of the highway that goes up from Bethʹel to Sheʹchem and toward the south of Le·boʹnah.”

7122.label: Judges 21:20
7122.text: So they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying: “Go, and YOU must lie in wait in the vineyards.

7123.label: Judges 21:21
7123.text: And YOU must look, and, there now, when the daughters of Shiʹloh come on out to dance in circle dances, YOU must also come out from the vineyards and carry off for yourselves by force each one his wife from the daughters of Shiʹloh, and YOU must go to the land of Benjamin.

7124.label: Judges 21:22
7124.text: And it must occur that should their fathers or their brothers come to conduct a legal case against us, we also shall certainly say to them, ‘Do us a favor for their sakes, because we have not taken for each one his wife by war, for it was not YOU that did the giving to them at a time when YOU would become guilty.’”

7125.label: Judges 21:23
7125.text: Accordingly the sons of Benjamin did just that way, and they proceeded to carry off wives for their number from the women dancing around, whom they snatched away; after which they went off and returned to their inheritance and built the cities and took up dwelling in them.

7126.label: Judges 21:24
7126.text: And the sons of Israel began to disperse from there at that time, each one to his own tribe and his own family; and they went their way out from there, each one to his own inheritance.

7127.label: Judges 21:25
7127.text: In those days there was no king in Israel. What was right in his own eyes was what each one was accustomed to do.
